display_title: [XLA:BufferAssignment] Add FAST_MULTI_SWEEP: a fast algorithm that uses less memory than FAST_MERGE.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:BufferAssignment] Add FAST_MULTI_SWEEP: a fast algorithm that uses less memory than FAST_MERGE.

FAST_MULTI_SWEEP runs FAST_MERGE and a new heap algorithm, `MultiSweepHeap`,
and keeps the result with the smaller heap. So it never uses more memory than
FAST_MERGE, and like FAST_MERGE it takes O(n log n) time for n buffers.

`MultiSweepHeap` (`xla/service/heap_simulator/multi_sweep_heap.h`) packs the
buffers in 16 ways and keeps the packing with the smallest heap. Like
FAST_MERGE, each packing goes through time once and puts every colocation
group, as one block, into the smallest free space that fits. In addition:

*   **Gaps:** a group's memory is not reserved for the whole time from its
    first member's start to its last member's end. While none of its members
    is live, other buffers that are freed in time can use it, alone or together
    with the free memory right below and above it.
*   **Directions:** a packing goes forward in time (like FAST_MERGE), backward,
    or both ways from a peak, after stacking the buffers that are live at the
    peak.
*   **Sides:** in a free chunk outside gaps, a buffer goes to the low end, or
    next to the buffer that is freed closest in time to it.

The packings to try can be chosen (`MultiSweepHeap::Packing`); buffer
assignment uses all 16. The result is deterministic.

This only adds the algorithm: nothing uses it unless it is selected. Like
FAST_MERGE and FAST_SPLIT, it honors `xla_multiheap_size_constraint_per_heap`,
and colors that don't support fast buffer assignment use DEFAULT instead. The
fallback logic doesn't change: with the fallback on, FAST_MULTI_SWEEP is
followed by the fallback algorithms, like SPATIAL and TEMPORAL.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1020109091

display_title: [ROCm] Add ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration into the ROCm tracer (PR2)

head_commit.message:
[ROCm profiler] Add rocm_tracer_options_utils

Second of three changes to support ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration
in the ROCm tracer. Adds the parser; nothing calls it yet.

UpdateRocmTracerOptionsFromProfilerOptions applies the gpu_* keys over
the caller's defaults and returns every problem as an error or warning,
instead of stopping at the first one as CUPTI does.
AppendOptionDiagnostics writes them to XSpace.errors/warnings and the
log.

- Event and annotation limits: a negative value is an error. For the two
  event limits, 0 means no limit, as on CUDA; passed through, it would
  empty the trace. gpu_max_annotation_strings = 0 retains none, as on
  CUDA, and draws a warning. gpu_max_activity_api_events is stored but
  not enforced yet, because the collector only counts HIP_API activity
  events; a warning says so.
- gpu_num_chips_to_profile_per_task: 0 or more than the device count
  means every GPU, as on CUDA. A negative value is an error. A smaller
  value draws a warning that every GPU is still traced.
- Keys CUPTI implements but ROCm does not draw a "not implemented"
  warning, whatever their value.
- Unknown gpu_* keys are errors. Other keys belong to other profiler
  components and are ignored.

RocmTraceCollectorImpl counts events in uint64_t guarded by
event_maps_mutex_, which every access already holds, instead of
std::atomic<int>, so a limit above INT_MAX no longer wraps the counter.

EveryCuptiKeyIsRecognized keeps the two key lists in sync: it reads the
CUPTI parser's source and fails if ROCm neither applies nor warns about
one of its keys. The RocmTraceCollectorOptions comments drop "if -1, no
limit".

Tests: rocm_tracer_options_utils_test, 25 host-only cases.

display_title: Fix spatial-minor backward weight conv rewrite on v6e+

head_commit.message:
Fix spatial-minor backward weight conv rewrite on v6e+

When `SpaceToBatchConverter` propagates a space-to-batch split into a
backward-weight (`window_dilation`) convolution, it folds the split into
`input_feature` and appends a size-1 spatial dimension, turning a 2D convolution
into a 3D spatial convolution. For small-batch and small-input-feature 2D
backward-weight convolutions (`BF16` or `F32`, filter area at most 64) that can
be lowered directly in a spatial-minor layout, this rank change prevents
downstream rewrites from matching the convolution and forces a fallback to
spatial-major layouts with expensive layout-conversion copies.

So this change adds `disable_backprop_filter_propagation_max_batch_size` to
`SpaceToBatchController` in `xla/service/space_to_batch_converter.h` to skip
propagating space-to-batch splits into eligible 2D backward-weight convolutions,
while continuing to propagate splits into unstrided, high-padded, large-filter,
or unsupported-layout convolutions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018243846

head_commit.message:
PR #52641: [XLA:FFI] Expose communicator rank and size through collectives

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52641

FFI host launch setup can borrow an XLA communicator but cannot read its rank and size through the public API. Expose metadata XLA already resolves so callers can select per-rank work without an additional NCCL query.

Add `Communicator::GetCommunicatorWithRankInfo(group_mode, groups, communication_id)`, returning the borrowed `communicator` handle, communicator-local `rank`, and total `size`. Keep `GetCommunicator()` as the existing handle-only query. Both use the same resolved clique.

Retain compatibility with the 0.2 C ABI for six months starting December 1, 2026. Compatibility code may be removed on or after June 1, 2027.

Executable placement (`replica_id`, `partition_id`, and their counts) is separated into !898 through the core invocation context. This MR has no dependency on that change. Process-local participant counts are not exposed.

**Validation**

External and internal wrapper tests cover returned metadata, forwarded group configuration, version handling, callback errors, and handle-only compatibility. A dedicated GPU test checks reversed participant ordering by returning each queried rank as a scalar, alongside truncated metadata arguments, untouched trailing fields, and undersized arguments. The existing public all-reduce test retains its original group helper and handle-only lookup. Source review and changed-line formatting are complete. On ComputeLab, six external API tests and two internal wrapper tests passed, and the CUDA backend library built before the final struct-size tightening. The updated two-GPU regression has not run: the ComputeLab request remained queued and was cancelled.

The focused handle-only compatibility test also passed on ComputeLab after switching to full-size arguments.

Let host launch setup read replica and partition coordinates and counts from the execution device assignment, without querying a communicator or transferring a scalar from the device.

--
4ba2ab5be915ccbccc6428d2636dc507dbe9644c by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA] Scope logical device lookup to the collectives extension

Expose logical coordinates through the existing GPU collective context and advance its extension version to 0.3. Remove the base FFI API and CPU changes while preserving lazy host-side lookup without requesting communication resources.

--
11c2f4ec4ffe2dbbe82ff91f6eb304b2d511df56 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA] Keep logical device docs scoped to the collectives API

Remove the standalone custom-call guide section because the guide does not otherwise document the collectives extension. Keep the accessor contract in its API headers.

--
054311ecf9109ffffed7796882cff0b0d52e5def by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA] Remove redundant extension null check from logical device lookup

--
1d6ff27d22ddde0a738d0f7a1ce7b6f642b8933d by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Expose communicator layout through the FFI collectives extension

Let host launch setup query communicator rank, size, and process-local participant count without acquiring a communicator or calling NCCL. Preserve group order and cover the metadata in the wrapper and runtime stage tests.

--

--
34117b6b0b7ee092cbd32e3354ea81df703f988a by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Preserve communicator-only FFI argument compatibility

Accept the original communicator argument prefix and write metadata only when the caller provides space. Exercise the smaller prefix and reject undersized arguments in the GPU all-reduce test.

--
380daac31fd5df47b2f1cbf581f6a7b596c6d89d by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Gate communicator metadata on the complete struct extent

--

Remove redundant communicator compatibility documentation

--
00c338b954f230993f767aae2c35acb8dba54b6d by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Preserve the handle-only C++ communicator API

Restore GetCommunicator and add GetCommunicatorWithRankInfo for metadata. Keep handle lookup available on 0.2 runtimes and verify both APIs through the internal and external wrappers.

--
00bbcd62c4c087c7af706d50a2ee038dcf401dbc by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Match the communicator metadata type to its query name

--
c28089d414cd055d8e1847c2f30851cac60fbc83 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Provide command buffer requests in the logical device test

Follow the updated Prepare contract so logical device validation reaches its handler in each runtime stage.

--
4e9c843cb8ace667c8dcca2fdb0f4d603a2d62e3 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Keep collective metadata scoped to communicator rank and size

Split executable placement into an independent core API change and remove the process-local participant count. Collective queries retain handle-only compatibility and no longer depend on placement metadata.

--
ec5447281d8bdf8b96323828c47d260d26862cb9 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Test reversed communicator ranks separately from all-reduce

Restore the original public all-reduce helper and handle-only lookup. Check queried ranks and ABI argument compatibility in a dedicated GPU test, returning each rank as a scalar result.

--
bbe0722f672941b2735429da7f7d9f0cbca32d09 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Remove custom collective version compatibility logic

Use the shared extension decoder policy and remove the metadata minor-version gate, compatibility tests, and unused test dependencies.

--
c9a725670dad8b1aab4b2ce93f74527f584d86a1 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Restore collective version compatibility handling

Restore Support, the metadata version guard, and their tests to retain compatible-minor handling for collective calls.

--
23d195b98b7c319fe31eb7466d05bad98f62dbac by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Validate communicator metadata and argument layouts

Reject incompatible extension versions, incomplete argument layouts, and invalid rank/size results before publishing outputs. Retain the 0.2 ABI for the six-month compatibility window ending 2027-06-01.

--
c27e152b6d1f9d5760d07b99a8a24857f438b84e by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Pass full communicator arguments for handle-only lookup

Initialize rank and size to -1 and advertise the current argument layout so runtimes can populate metadata when available. Keep the handle-only return value and test compatibility with older callbacks that leave metadata unset.

--
31bffc6c2b2ac86641fdb3dd857bcda07bb1f85c by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Validate legacy argument size before checking rank fields

Reject undersized communicator arguments explicitly so has_rank_info can use a greater-than comparison while preserving legacy and full-layout validation.

--
3d526151a04c039ad44283b73066d50c32503b9b by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Consolidate versioned communicator argument validation

Name the v0.2 and v0.3 layouts explicitly and validate the selected minimum size once. Gate rank metadata on the complete v0.3 layout while preserving rejection of undersized and partial arguments.

Merging this change closes #52641

head_commit.message:
PR #52820: [XLA:GPU] Work around large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52820

📝 Summary of Changes
Fixes #48979, a JAX/XLA regression.

Large POSIX-FD CUDA VMM allocations can fail with OUT_OF_MEMORY on WSL
despite sufficient free memory. Try the full allocation first, then retry
eligible WSL failures with backing allocations of at most 1 GiB mapped into
one contiguous address range.

Back contiguous device allocations with 1 GiB physical chunks on WSL
when POSIX-FD handles are enabled and fabric/multicast are unavailable.
This avoids the driver failure for large exportable allocations while
preserving sharing support.

Preserve POSIX-FD exportability for multi-GPU sharing. Other platforms keep
their existing allocation path. Locality-domain allocations, enabled FABRIC
handles, and multicast-capable devices are excluded from chunk retries.

Adds a manual 6 GiB plus padding allocator regression and a two-GPU NCCL
large-buffer registration/transfer test. Both check data around every GiB
boundary; the allocator test also checks POSIX-FD handle properties.

Disabling enable_posix_fd_handle would be a shorter workaround, but would
remove POSIX-FD export needed by cross-process GPU sharing and some NCCL
paths. Keep exportable allocations to preserve multi-GPU support under WSL2.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No perf improvements

🧪 Unit Tests:

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight allocator tests, the 6 GiB regression,
formatting, and error-injection checks pass. Three locality-domain tests
skip for version/hardware requirements. The two-GPU NCCL test compiled but
skipped on this one-GPU host. RDMA-enabled cases were not run.

🧪 Execution Tests:
None

[XLA:GPU] Retry large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

WSL can reject large POSIX-FD VMM allocations with OUT_OF_MEMORY despite
sufficient free memory. Try the full-size allocation first, then retry
with backing chunks of at most 1 GiB on WSL with fabric handles disabled
and multicast unsupported. Exclude locality-domain allocations and map the
chunks into one contiguous virtual address range.

Keep POSIX-FD exportability to preserve multi-GPU support under WSL2.
Disabling enable_posix_fd_handle would be shorter, but removes handles
needed by cross-process GPU sharing and some NCCL paths.

Retain only the original first handle and release later creation
references after mapping. Track the mapped prefix for rollback and keep
the existing deallocation path.

Add a manual 6 GiB plus padding allocator regression and a WSL-only NCCL
regression that registers independent 6 GiB buffers, transfers the full
buffer, and checks both sides of each 1 GiB boundary. Skip the NCCL test
before GPU discovery on other operating systems and retain hardware,
memory, and chunking checks.

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight non-RDMA allocator tests, the manual
6 GiB regression, clang-format 17.0.6, and git diff --check pass. Three
upstream locality tests skip for version or hardware requirements. The
full two-GPU NCCL test skips on this single-GPU machine. Earlier local
two-process probes transferred a 6 GiB chunked source into an independent
256 MiB receiver; write and forced peer-read paths passed. The read probe
refreshed source registration per window and confirmed two-segment
imports at all five boundaries. Distinct-GPU execution remains untested.

[XLA:GPU] Clarify WSL retries and generalize the NCCL regression

Make the large-buffer NCCL registration test check allocation, registration,
and full-buffer transfer across supported CUDA hosts without requiring WSL
or a particular physical mapping shape. Remove the unused detection and
mapping dependencies.

Use individual eligibility checks inside the WSL retry path, preserving
original status codes and messages while explaining why retries are not
eligible. Return non-OOM allocation failures directly and explicitly guard
the chunk-mapping loop with IsWsl().

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight allocator tests, the manual 6 GiB
regression, clang-format 17.0.6, and git diff --check pass. Fault injection
confirms original non-OOM errors are returned and neither native Linux nor
failed OS detection triggers chunk retries. Three locality-domain tests skip
for version/hardware requirements. The two-GPU NCCL regression compiles but
skips on this single-GPU host; RDMA-enabled cases were not run.

head_commit.message:
PR #53153: [ROCM] Refactoring group gemm helper functions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53153

## Summary of Changes

Cleans up the ROCm grouped/ragged-dot "update user arguments" helper that
populates the device-side `hipblaslt_ext::UserArguments` array, with no change
to the generated device code in the normal operating range.

- **Collapsed three near-identical kernels into one.**
  `SetUserArgsKernelRaggedIn{NonContracting,Contracting,Batch}Dim` were ~95%
  duplicated. They are now a single mode-templated
  `SetUserArgsKernel<T, gpu::RaggedDotMode Mode>`; the only per-mode
  differences (the `m`/`n`/`k`/`batch` assignment and whether the per-gemm
  index or the running prefix-sum offset drives each pointer) are handled with
  `if constexpr (Mode)`. The shared block-scan prefix-sum loop and the common
  `UserArguments` fill (`FillCommonUserArgs`) now exist once.

- **Replaced two ~35-argument signatures with POD structs.**
  The kernel now takes a single by-value `GroupGemmKernelArgs`, and the host
  entry point takes `const GroupGemmUpdateArgsParams&` instead of ~35 scalar
  arguments.

- **Premultiply strides by element byte width on the host.**
  Offset strides are converted to byte strides on the host (element stride
  times the operand's element width, after the operand swap), so the kernel's
  `OffsetPtr` no longer needs a per-element `log2` shift.

- **Hardened the ragged-dimension prefix sum against 32-bit overflow.**
  The global prefix-sum carry (`cumulative_offset` / `offset_group`) and
  `OffsetPtr`'s index are now 64-bit, so a ragged-dimension total exceeding
  `2^32` elements no longer wraps. The within-chunk `BlockScan` stays 32-bit
  (bounded by a single 256-wide chunk). The first-chunk special case in the
  carry computation was also removed as redundant.

- **Tidied `copy_shared_to_global`.**
  Const-correct source pointers and a simpler remainder loop.

- **Decoupled the device helper from the `BlasLt` class header.**
  `GroupGemmUpdateArgsParams` and the `GroupGemmUpdateArgs` declaration now
  live in `hip_blas_lt_helper.h` (next to the `.cu.cc` that defines them)
  rather than `hip_blas_lt.h`. Kernel dispatch over
  `(RaggedDotMode, group-size byte width)` uses a small local macro.

## Justification

The three kernels had diverged into large copy-paste blocks that were hard to
keep in sync, and the matching ~35-argument launch/host signatures were
error-prone to edit. Consolidating them removes ~460 lines while producing the
same specialized kernels. The 64-bit carry additionally fixes a latent overflow
for very large grouped/ragged dots (total ragged extent > ~4.29e9 elements),
where the carry can overflow even while each individual `m`/`n`/`k` still fits
in 32 bits.

display_title: PR #52641: [XLA:FFI] Expose communicator rank and size through collectives

head_commit.message:
PR #52641: [XLA:FFI] Expose communicator rank and size through collectives

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52641

FFI host launch setup can borrow an XLA communicator but cannot read its rank and size through the public API. Expose metadata XLA already resolves so callers can select per-rank work without an additional NCCL query.

Add `Communicator::GetCommunicatorWithRankInfo(group_mode, groups, communication_id)`, returning the borrowed `communicator` handle, communicator-local `rank`, and total `size`. Keep `GetCommunicator()` as the existing handle-only query. Both use the same resolved clique.

Retain compatibility with the 0.2 C ABI for six months starting December 1, 2026. Compatibility code may be removed on or after June 1, 2027.

Executable placement (`replica_id`, `partition_id`, and their counts) is separated into !898 through the core invocation context. This MR has no dependency on that change. Process-local participant counts are not exposed.

**Validation**

External and internal wrapper tests cover returned metadata, forwarded group configuration, version handling, callback errors, and handle-only compatibility. A dedicated GPU test checks reversed participant ordering by returning each queried rank as a scalar, alongside truncated metadata arguments, untouched trailing fields, and undersized arguments. The existing public all-reduce test retains its original group helper and handle-only lookup. Source review and changed-line formatting are complete. On ComputeLab, six external API tests and two internal wrapper tests passed, and the CUDA backend library built before the final struct-size tightening. The updated two-GPU regression has not run: the ComputeLab request remained queued and was cancelled.

The focused handle-only compatibility test also passed on ComputeLab after switching to full-size arguments.

head_commit.message:
PR #53153: [ROCM] Refactoring group gemm helper functions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53153

## Summary of Changes

Cleans up the ROCm grouped/ragged-dot "update user arguments" helper that
populates the device-side `hipblaslt_ext::UserArguments` array, with no change
to the generated device code in the normal operating range.

- **Collapsed three near-identical kernels into one.**
  `SetUserArgsKernelRaggedIn{NonContracting,Contracting,Batch}Dim` were ~95%
  duplicated. They are now a single mode-templated
  `SetUserArgsKernel<T, gpu::RaggedDotMode Mode>`; the only per-mode
  differences (the `m`/`n`/`k`/`batch` assignment and whether the per-gemm
  index or the running prefix-sum offset drives each pointer) are handled with
  `if constexpr (Mode)`. The shared block-scan prefix-sum loop and the common
  `UserArguments` fill (`FillCommonUserArgs`) now exist once.

- **Replaced two ~35-argument signatures with POD structs.**
  The kernel now takes a single by-value `GroupGemmKernelArgs`, and the host
  entry point takes `const GroupGemmUpdateArgsParams&` instead of ~35 scalar
  arguments.

- **Premultiply strides by element byte width on the host.**
  Offset strides are converted to byte strides on the host (element stride
  times the operand's element width, after the operand swap), so the kernel's
  `OffsetPtr` no longer needs a per-element `log2` shift.

- **Hardened the ragged-dimension prefix sum against 32-bit overflow.**
  The global prefix-sum carry (`cumulative_offset` / `offset_group`) and
  `OffsetPtr`'s index are now 64-bit, so a ragged-dimension total exceeding
  `2^32` elements no longer wraps. The within-chunk `BlockScan` stays 32-bit
  (bounded by a single 256-wide chunk). The first-chunk special case in the
  carry computation was also removed as redundant.

- **Tidied `copy_shared_to_global`.**
  Const-correct source pointers and a simpler remainder loop.

- **Decoupled the device helper from the `BlasLt` class header.**
  `GroupGemmUpdateArgsParams` and the `GroupGemmUpdateArgs` declaration now
  live in `hip_blas_lt_helper.h` (next to the `.cu.cc` that defines them)
  rather than `hip_blas_lt.h`. Kernel dispatch over
  `(RaggedDotMode, group-size byte width)` uses a small local macro.

## Justification

The three kernels had diverged into large copy-paste blocks that were hard to
keep in sync, and the matching ~35-argument launch/host signatures were
error-prone to edit. Consolidating them removes ~460 lines while producing the
same specialized kernels. The 64-bit carry additionally fixes a latent overflow
for very large grouped/ragged dots (total ragged extent > ~4.29e9 elements),
where the carry can overflow even while each individual `m`/`n`/`k` still fits
in 32 bits.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove use_dlls flags from WORKSPACE absl and protobuf patches

Only TensorFlow's Windows config sets the `use_dlls` flags, and TensorFlow's Windows build now requires Bzlmod. The Bzlmod build takes these flags from TensorFlow's own absl and protobuf patches, so the copies that XLA applies in WORKSPACE builds are dead.

Delete `build_dll.patch` for absl, which only added the flag. In `protobuf.patch`, drop the flag, its `config_setting`, and the `local_defines` that depend on it. The other protobuf hunks stay, including the Windows changes that do not depend on the flag.

head_commit.message:
PR #52641: [XLA:FFI] Expose communicator rank and size through collectives

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52641

FFI host launch setup can borrow an XLA communicator but cannot read its rank and size through the public API. Expose metadata XLA already resolves so callers can select per-rank work without an additional NCCL query.

Add `Communicator::GetCommunicatorWithRankInfo(group_mode, groups, communication_id)`, returning the borrowed `communicator` handle, communicator-local `rank`, and total `size`. Keep `GetCommunicator()` as the existing handle-only query. Both use the same resolved clique.

Retain compatibility with the 0.2 C ABI for six months starting December 1, 2026. Compatibility code may be removed on or after June 1, 2027.

Executable placement (`replica_id`, `partition_id`, and their counts) is separated into !898 through the core invocation context. This MR has no dependency on that change. Process-local participant counts are not exposed.

**Validation**

External and internal wrapper tests cover returned metadata, forwarded group configuration, version handling, callback errors, and handle-only compatibility. A dedicated GPU test checks reversed participant ordering by returning each queried rank as a scalar, alongside truncated metadata arguments, untouched trailing fields, and undersized arguments. The existing public all-reduce test retains its original group helper and handle-only lookup. Source review and changed-line formatting are complete. On ComputeLab, six external API tests and two internal wrapper tests passed, and the CUDA backend library built before the final struct-size tightening. The updated two-GPU regression has not run: the ComputeLab request remained queued and was cancelled.

The focused handle-only compatibility test also passed on ComputeLab after switching to full-size arguments.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Move CTA cluster dimensions into LaunchDimensions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Move CTA cluster dimensions into LaunchDimensions

CTA cluster dimensions (`se::ClusterDim`) were previously tracked in separate
fields alongside `LaunchDimensions` across `GpuKernelSpec`, `KernelReuseCache`,
and `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`, and `AnnotateKernelLaunchDimensions` did
not emit the `"nvvm.cluster_dim"` LLVM function attribute.

Fold optional `cluster_dims` directly into `LaunchDimensions` and
`LaunchDimensionsProto` as a `constexpr` property to prepare for clustered GPU
kernel emitters:
- Validate in `AnnotateKernelLaunchDimensions` that `cluster_dims` is only set
  on Hopper+ NVPTX targets, has strictly positive dimensions, and evenly
  divides `block_counts`, and attach `"nvvm.cluster_dim"` to the kernel
  function.
- Remove the duplicate `cluster_dim` fields from `GpuKernelSpec` (reserving
  field 7 in `GpuKernelSpecProto`), `KernelReuseCache` (serializing 3D
  `LaunchDimensionsProto` in `CompilationCacheEntryProto` and bumping
  `kCacheCompatibilityVersion`), and `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`, reading
  `launch_dimensions().cluster_dims()` instead.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Dump progress on GPU device execution timeouts

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Dump progress on GPU device execution timeouts

Previously, `--xla_gpu_execution_progress_tracking` only wired its progress dump to the host-side terminate watchdog (`--xla_gpu_execution_terminate_timeout`). When a kernel or collective hung on the device after host dispatch returned (`--xla_gpu_device_execution_terminate_timeout` or `ExecutionTimeoutHandler`), the process aborted without logging completed or pending thunks, and `ScopedProgressTracker` on the host stack was destroyed before in-flight device work finished (returning `EventPool` events while they were still pending on the stream).

This change:
1. Extracts `LogExecutionProgress` and `ReleaseProgressTracker` (serialized across threads by `GetProgressLogMutex()` with `[<device_ordinal>]` prefixes on every line, and logging nested `kCommandBuffer` thunks for pending command buffers).
2. Wires `LogExecutionProgress` (via `std::weak_ptr<ProgressTracker>`) to `HangWatchdog::Abort` for both host and device terminate timeouts as well as `ExecutionTimeoutGuards`.
3. Keeps `ProgressTracker` alive in `main_stream->DoHostCallback` (and on early error paths via `cleanup_progress_tracker`) until enqueued device work completes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022685940

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Snapshot ThunkMetadata and nested CommandBuffer thunks in ProgressTracker

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Snapshot ThunkMetadata and nested CommandBuffer thunks in ProgressTracker

Previously, `ProgressTracker` stored raw `const Thunk*` pointers in `ThunkExecutionEvent` to read `thunk->kind()` and `thunk->profile_annotation()` (as an `absl::string_view`) when formatting progress dumps. If `ProgressTracker` outlives host dispatch via `ScopedProgressTracker::tracker()` to track in-flight device execution, destroying `GpuExecutable` before device execution finishes would leave dangling `const Thunk*` pointers and string views. In addition, when a `CommandBufferThunk` was pending, `ProgressTracker` only recorded the outer `kCommandBuffer` thunk without its nested HLO thunks.

This change snapshots owning `ThunkMetadata` (`thunk_idx`, `kind`, `name`, and `nested_thunks` for `kCommandBuffer` thunks) during `InstallProgressTracker` and stores `thunk_idx` indices in `ThunkExecutionEvent` so `ProgressTracker` never dereferences `const Thunk*` pointers after `ExecuteOnStream`.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Split flag registration in MakeDebugOptionsFlags into smaller stack frames.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Split flag registration in MakeDebugOptionsFlags into smaller stack frames.

**Status quo:** `MakeDebugOptionsFlags` in `xla/debug_options_flags.cc`
registers all ~430 flags in a single function. In unoptimized builds every
`tsl::Flag` temporary gets its own stack slot, so the stack frame grows with
every flag. It has now crossed 200 KB, which breaks toolchains that build with
`-Wframe-larger-than=200000 -Werror`.

**Why:** Any new flag tipped it over the limit; the latest one did. Besides the
build break, a ~200 KB frame is also risky when the flags are first parsed on a
thread with a small stack.

**Design choices:** The `flag_list->push_back(...)` calls are moved, unchanged,
into three immediately invoked `[&] { ... }();` lambdas. Each lambda is its own
function with its own frame (~70 KB each), and only one is live at a time. The
`[&]` capture keeps all existing setter helpers in scope, so no flag definition
changes. The setters already capture `debug_options` by value, so nothing stored
in a `tsl::Flag` refers to the lambdas. Optimized builds may inline the lambdas
again, which is fine since stack slots are reused there.

**Compromises:** The registration body is indented by two more spaces, which
makes the diff large (whitespace and re-wrapped help strings only; no flag
name, default, setter, or help text changed). Pending changes touching this
function will need a rebase.

**Alternatives:** (1) Suppressing `-Wframe-larger-than` for this target hides
a real ~200 KB frame. (2) Rolling back the latest flag addition only defers the
problem to the next flag. (3) Moving the setters into a registrar class with
one member function per chunk avoids reindentation but rewrites ~50 setter
helpers and their uses; more invasive for the same effect.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023647948

display_title: [PjRt-IFRT] Validate HloSharding invariants in HloShardingSpec

head_commit.message:
[PjRt-IFRT] Validate HloSharding invariants in HloShardingSpec

`xla::HloSharding` permits tuple shardings and sparse nonnegative explicit
device IDs (`device >= num_devices`), neither of which is valid for
`ifrt::HloShardingSpec` or `ifrt::HloSharding` (where explicit tiled device IDs
index `[0, num_shards)`). In addition, `Unknown` shardings are accepted at
construction, but hit `CHECK` failures instead of returning an error in
`IndexDomains`, `UniqueIndexDomains`, and `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex`.

Reject tuple `xla::HloSharding`s and explicit tiled device IDs outside
`[0, num_shards)` in `HloShardingSpec::CreateIfValid`, and return
`InvalidArgumentError` for `Unknown` shardings in `IndexDomains`,
`UniqueIndexDomains`, and `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex`.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

This is another one that _could_ be considered a candidate for ShapeTracker, which I am working on in parallel (see chain of cls after cl/1022689285). However, having a use case might make it easier to find bugs when I do this and this is only 177 lines.

Slices are tracked alongside the ShapeTracker as per-dimension ranges of the port of the dot: the ShapeTracker describes the unsliced tensor, and the ranges become the `slices` of the cuDNN tensor. Nested slices are combined.

A slice can be followed by shape transformations before it reaches the dot, e.g. `dot(transpose(slice(p)), ...)`. When a slice is reached, it is moved to the port side of the ShapeTracker (next to the dot): the steps of the ShapeTracker are replayed on the shape of the operand of the slice, carrying the sliced range of every dimension along.

Limitations:
- for merged dimensions, only the major-most dimension of a group can be sliced (otherwise you can't represent them as one stride, one range per dimension),
- for split dimensions, the range has to be aligned to the dimensions that it is split into,
- slices cannot be strided,
- slices can be in the prologue, but not epilogue (cudnn fails to execute epilogue slices with CUDNN_STATUS_BAD_PARAM_NULL_POINTER)

head_commit.message:
PR #52443: [XLA:GPU] Add support probe and dense fallback for cuDNN ragged-dot fusion

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52443

📝 Summary of Changes

Make the cuDNN ragged-dot fusion fall back to the regular dense expansion when
cuDNN cannot build a plan for a given ragged dot. The fusion stays behind
`xla_gpu_experimental_use_ragged_dot_fusion`, whose default is unchanged.

- `RaggedDotRewriter` takes an optional `is_supported_by_cudnn_fusion` callback.
  A ragged dot that passes the existing static gates (cuDNN version, Ampere+,
  binary libraries enabled, unbatched 2D lhs / 2D-3D rhs / 1D group sizes,
  F16/BF16 types, single ragged dim) is only left for the fusion rewriter if
  the callback also returns true; otherwise it is expanded to dense dot as before.
  The decision has to be made here because `RaggedDotRewriter` runs before layout
  assignment, while `RaggedDotFusionRewriter` runs post-layout, where a dense
  expansion would produce layout-less ops.
- New `IsRaggedDotSupportedByCuDnn` (`ragged_dot_cudnn_support.{h,cc}`, CUDA-only):
  builds a scratch module with the ragged dot, runs `RaggedDotFusionRewriter`,
  and asks cuDNN about the resulting fusion via `ResolveCudnnSupport` +
  `GetAvailablePlanCount(...) > 0`, for both JIT and deviceless compilation
  (honoring `xla_gpu_cudnn_deviceless_compilation_mode`). Only a positive answer
  counts as supported; no plans and errors all fall back to dense, with the
  reason logged at `VLOG(3)`.
- Plumbing: virtual `GpuCompiler::IsRaggedDotSupportedByCuDnn` (default
  `Decision::Forbid`, overridden in `NVPTXCompiler`). `RunOptimizationPasses` now
  receives the `StreamExecutor*` and derives `is_deviceless` from it.

🎯 Justification

With `xla_gpu_experimental_use_ragged_dot_fusion` enabled, a ragged dot that
passes the static gates but that cuDNN has no engine for (e.g. mixed
token/weight dtypes) fails compilation hard in the cuDNN fusion compiler. With
this change such a ragged dot compiles via the dense path instead, so the flag
can be turned on safely later.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `RaggedDotRewriterTest.CudnnSupportCallbackDecidesFusionOrExpansion`: with the
  fusion enabled, a callback returning true leaves the ragged dot in place; a
  callback returning false expands it to dense.
- `RaggedDotRewriterTest.ExpandsWhenBinaryLibrariesDisabled`.
- `ragged_dot_cudnn_support_test`: supported and unsupported ragged dots.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Snapshot ThunkMetadata and nested CommandBuffer thunks in ProgressTracker

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Snapshot ThunkMetadata and nested CommandBuffer thunks in ProgressTracker

Previously, `ThunkExecutor::ScopedProgressTracker` owned `ProgressTracker` via `std::unique_ptr`, and `ProgressTracker` stored raw `const Thunk*` pointers in `ThunkExecutionEvent` to read `thunk->kind()` and `thunk->profile_annotation()` when formatting progress dumps. If `ProgressTracker` outlives host dispatch to track in-flight device execution, destroying `GpuExecutable` before device execution finishes would leave dangling `const Thunk*` pointers. In addition, when a `CommandBufferThunk` was pending, `ProgressTracker` only recorded the outer `kCommandBuffer` thunk without its nested HLO thunks.

This change:
1. Converts `ScopedProgressTracker::tracker_` to `std::shared_ptr<ProgressTracker>` so callers can retain `ProgressTracker` until enqueued stream work completes while `ScopedProgressTracker` still manages thread-local installation during `ExecuteOnStream`.
2. Snapshots `ThunkMetadata` (`thunk_idx`, `kind`, `name`, and `nested_thunks` for `kCommandBuffer` thunks) during `InstallProgressTracker` so `ProgressTracker` never dereferences `const Thunk*` pointers after `InstallProgressTracker`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022769146

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Dump progress on GPU device execution timeouts

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Dump progress on GPU device execution timeouts

Previously, `--xla_gpu_execution_progress_tracking` only wired its progress dump to the host-side terminate watchdog (`--xla_gpu_execution_terminate_timeout`). When a kernel or collective hung on the device after host dispatch returned (`--xla_gpu_device_execution_terminate_timeout` or `ExecutionTimeoutHandler`), the process aborted without logging completed or pending thunks, and `ScopedProgressTracker` on the host stack was destroyed before in-flight device work finished (returning `EventPool` events while they were still pending on the stream).

This change:
1. Extracts `LogExecutionProgress` and `ReleaseProgressTracker` (serialized across threads by `GetProgressLogMutex()` with `[<device_ordinal>]` prefixes on every line, and logging nested `kCommandBuffer` thunks for pending command buffers).
2. Wires `LogExecutionProgress` (via `std::weak_ptr<ProgressTracker>`) to `HangWatchdog::Abort` for both host and device terminate timeouts as well as `ExecutionTimeoutGuards`.
3. Keeps `ProgressTracker` alive in `main_stream->DoHostCallback` (and on early error paths via `cleanup_progress_tracker`) until enqueued device work completes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022685940

display_title: Remove obsolete acquire memory fence from `PopAnnotation()`.

head_commit.message:
Remove obsolete acquire memory fence from `PopAnnotation()`.

`PopAnnotation()` executed an unconditional `std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire)` on every scope exit even when both `AnnotationStack` and NVTX were disabled. That fence worked around a 2019 header-only `thread_local` DSO split that was resolved when `AnnotationStack` moved out-of-line, and emitted an unnecessary `dmb ishld` barrier on `aarch64` CPUs on every thunk or command destructor.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Move CTA cluster dimensions into LaunchDimensions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Move CTA cluster dimensions into LaunchDimensions

CTA cluster dimensions (`se::ClusterDim`) were previously tracked in separate
fields alongside `LaunchDimensions` across `GpuKernelSpec`, `KernelReuseCache`,
and `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`, and `AnnotateKernelLaunchDimensions` did
not emit the `"nvvm.cluster_dim"` LLVM function attribute.

Fold optional `cluster_dims` directly into `LaunchDimensions` and
`LaunchDimensionsProto` as a `constexpr` property to prepare for clustered GPU
kernel emitters:
- Validate in `AnnotateKernelLaunchDimensions` that `cluster_dims` is only set
  on NVPTX targets, has strictly positive dimensions, and evenly divides
  `block_counts`, and attach `"nvvm.cluster_dim"` to the kernel function.
- Remove the duplicate `cluster_dim` fields from `GpuKernelSpec` (reserving
  field 7 in `GpuKernelSpecProto`), `KernelReuseCache::Entry`, and
  `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`, reading `launch_dimensions().cluster_dims()`
  instead.

display_title: PR #46400: [XLA:GPU] Use IEEE-754 compliant f32 division in NVPTX backend

head_commit.message:
PR #46400: [XLA:GPU] Use IEEE-754 compliant f32 division in NVPTX backend

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46400

#ai-generated

**Fixes:** #37181

**Summary of Changes**
Changed `-nvptx-prec-divf32` from `1` (`div.full`, 2 ULP error) to `2` (`div.rnd`, IEEE-754 compliant) in the NVPTX backend. LLVM already defaults to `2`; XLA was overriding it.

**Justification**
GPU float32 division produces non-IEEE-754 results: `a/a` evaluates to `0.99999994` instead of `1.0` for many f32 values. This violates user expectations and breaks numerical invariants. The issue was confirmed on RTX 3090 (JAX 0.6.0) in #37181.

**Kind of Contribution**
Bug Fix

**Benchmark**
N/A — this is a correctness fix, not a performance change. The original `=1` override was added for "float-division heavy benchmarks" but `div.full` trades correctness for speed; `div.rnd` is LLVM's default and is IEEE-754 compliant with >1 ULP accuracy.

**Unit Tests**
New regression test: `xla/tests/ieee_f32_division_test.cc` (registered as `//xla/tests:ieee_f32_division_test`, runs on cpu+gpu) asserts the IEEE-754 identity properties `x / x == 1.0` and `x / 1.0 == x` that the `div.full` override broke, across values including `FLT_MAX`, `FLT_MIN`, `1e10`, `1e-10`. It uses parameters and disabled fast math so the division is actually executed by the backend rather than folded or simplified away. Existing GPU backend tests continue to pass: `nvptx_backend_test`, `load_ir_module_test`, `utils_test`, `nvptx_utils_test`.

**Execution Tests**
A standalone reproducer script is available at `repro_xla_37181.py` that verifies IEEE-754 division compliance across 5 categories (identity, inverse, overflow, underflow, NaN).

display_title: [XLA] Split flag registration in MakeDebugOptionsFlags into smaller stack frames.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Split flag registration in MakeDebugOptionsFlags into smaller stack frames.

**Status quo:** `MakeDebugOptionsFlags` in `xla/debug_options_flags.cc`
registers all ~430 flags in a single function. In unoptimized builds every
`tsl::Flag` temporary gets its own stack slot, so the stack frame grows with
every flag. It has now crossed 200 KB, which breaks toolchains that build with
`-Wframe-larger-than=200000 -Werror`.

**Why:** Any new flag tipped it over the limit; the latest one did. Besides the
build break, a ~200 KB frame is also risky when the flags are first parsed on a
thread with a small stack.

**Design choices:** The `flag_list->push_back(...)` calls are moved, unchanged,
into three immediately invoked `[&] { ... }();` lambdas. Each lambda is its own
function with its own frame (~70 KB each), and only one is live at a time. The
`[&]` capture keeps all existing setter helpers in scope, so no flag definition
changes. The setters already capture `debug_options` by value, so nothing stored
in a `tsl::Flag` refers to the lambdas. Optimized builds may inline the lambdas
again, which is fine since stack slots are reused there.

**Compromises:** The registration body is indented by two more spaces, which
makes the diff large (whitespace and re-wrapped help strings only; no flag
name, default, setter, or help text changed). Pending changes touching this
function will need a rebase.

**Alternatives:** (1) Suppressing `-Wframe-larger-than` for this target hides
a real ~200 KB frame. (2) Rolling back the latest flag addition only defers the
problem to the next flag. (3) Moving the setters into a registrar class with
one member function per chunk avoids reindentation but rewrites ~50 setter
helpers and their uses; more invasive for the same effect.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023382718

display_title: Fix spatial-minor backward weight conv rewrite on v6e+

head_commit.message:
Fix spatial-minor backward weight conv rewrite on v6e+

When `SpaceToBatchConverter` propagates a space-to-batch split into a
backward-weight (`window_dilation`) convolution, it folds the split into
`input_feature` and appends a size-1 spatial dimension, turning a 2D convolution
into a 3D spatial convolution. For small-batch and small-input-feature 2D
backward-weight convolutions (`BF16` or `F32`, filter area at most 64) that can
be lowered directly in a spatial-minor layout, this rank change prevents
downstream rewrites from matching the convolution and forces a fallback to
spatial-major layouts with expensive layout-conversion copies.

So this change adds `disable_backprop_filter_propagation_max_batch_size` to
`SpaceToBatchController` in `xla/service/space_to_batch_converter.h` to skip
propagating space-to-batch splits into eligible 2D backward-weight convolutions,
while continuing to propagate splits into unstrided, high-padded, large-filter,
or unsupported-layout convolutions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018243846

display_title: PR #52641: [XLA:FFI] Expose communicator rank and size through collectives

head_commit.message:
PR #52641: [XLA:FFI] Expose communicator rank and size through collectives

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52641

FFI host launch setup can borrow an XLA communicator but cannot read its rank and size through the public API. Expose metadata XLA already resolves so callers can select per-rank work without an additional NCCL query.

Add `Communicator::GetCommunicatorWithRankInfo(group_mode, groups, communication_id)`, returning the borrowed `communicator` handle, communicator-local `rank`, and total `size`. Keep `GetCommunicator()` as the existing handle-only query. Both use the same resolved clique.

Retain compatibility with the 0.2 C ABI for six months starting December 1, 2026. Compatibility code may be removed on or after June 1, 2027.

Executable placement (`replica_id`, `partition_id`, and their counts) is separated into !898 through the core invocation context. This MR has no dependency on that change. Process-local participant counts are not exposed.

**Validation**

External and internal wrapper tests cover returned metadata, forwarded group configuration, version handling, callback errors, and handle-only compatibility. A dedicated GPU test checks reversed participant ordering by returning each queried rank as a scalar, alongside truncated metadata arguments, untouched trailing fields, and undersized arguments. The existing public all-reduce test retains its original group helper and handle-only lookup. Source review and changed-line formatting are complete. On ComputeLab, six external API tests and two internal wrapper tests passed, and the CUDA backend library built before the final struct-size tightening. The updated two-GPU regression has not run: the ComputeLab request remained queued and was cancelled.

The focused handle-only compatibility test also passed on ComputeLab after switching to full-size arguments.

Expose logical coordinates through the existing GPU collective context and advance its extension version to 0.3. Remove the base FFI API and CPU changes while preserving lazy host-side lookup without requesting communication resources.

4e9c843cb8ace667c8dcca2fdb0f4d603a2d62e3 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Split executable placement into an independent core API change and remove the process-local participant count. Collective queries retain handle-only compatibility and no longer depend on placement metadata.

--

--

--
23d195b98b7c319fe31eb7466d05bad98f62dbac by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Validate communicator metadata and argument layouts

Reject incompatible extension versions, incomplete argument layouts, and invalid rank/size results before publishing outputs. Retain the 0.2 ABI for the six-month compatibility window ending 2027-06-01.

--
c27e152b6d1f9d5760d07b99a8a24857f438b84e by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Initialize rank and size to -1 and advertise the current argument layout so runtimes can populate metadata when available. Keep the handle-only return value and test compatibility with older callbacks that leave metadata unset.

--

[XLA:FFI] Validate legacy argument size before checking rank fields

Reject undersized communicator arguments explicitly so has_rank_info can use a greater-than comparison while preserving legacy and full-layout validation.

--
3d526151a04c039ad44283b73066d50c32503b9b by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Consolidate versioned communicator argument validation

Name the v0.2 and v0.3 layouts explicitly and validate the selected minimum size once. Gate rank metadata on the complete v0.3 layout while preserving rejection of undersized and partial arguments.

- RocmExecutor::IsHostMemoryPinned left start_addr/range_size

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

This is another one that _could_ be considered a candidate for ShapeTracker, which I am working on in parallel (see chain of cls after cl/1022689285). However, having a use case might make it easier to find bugs when I do this and this is only 177 lines.

Slices are tracked alongside the ShapeTracker as per-dimension ranges of the port of the dot: the ShapeTracker describes the unsliced tensor, and the ranges become the `slices` of the cuDNN tensor. Nested slices are combined.

A slice can be followed by shape transformations before it reaches the dot, e.g. `dot(transpose(slice(p)), ...)`. When a slice is reached, it is moved to the port side of the ShapeTracker (next to the dot): the steps of the ShapeTracker are replayed on the shape of the operand of the slice, carrying the sliced range of every dimension along.

Limitations:
- for merged dimensions, only the major-most dimension of a group can be sliced (otherwise you can't represent them as one stride, one range per dimension),
- for split dimensions, the range has to be aligned to the dimensions that it is split into,
- slices cannot be strided,
- slices can be in the prologue, but not epilogue (cudnn fails to execute epilogue slices with CUDNN_STATUS_BAD_PARAM_NULL_POINTER)

head_commit.message:
PR #52641: [XLA:FFI] Expose communicator rank and size through collectives

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52641

FFI host launch setup can borrow an XLA communicator but cannot read its rank and size through the public API. Expose metadata XLA already resolves so callers can select per-rank work without an additional NCCL query.

Add `Communicator::GetCommunicatorWithRankInfo(group_mode, groups, communication_id)`, returning the borrowed `communicator` handle, communicator-local `rank`, and total `size`. Keep `GetCommunicator()` as the existing handle-only query. Both use the same resolved clique.

Retain compatibility with the 0.2 C ABI for six months starting December 1, 2026. Compatibility code may be removed on or after June 1, 2027.

Executable placement (`replica_id`, `partition_id`, and their counts) is separated into !898 through the core invocation context. This MR has no dependency on that change. Process-local participant counts are not exposed.

**Validation**

External and internal wrapper tests cover returned metadata, forwarded group configuration, version handling, callback errors, and handle-only compatibility. A dedicated GPU test checks reversed participant ordering by returning each queried rank as a scalar, alongside truncated metadata arguments, untouched trailing fields, and undersized arguments. The existing public all-reduce test retains its original group helper and handle-only lookup. Source review and changed-line formatting are complete. On ComputeLab, six external API tests and two internal wrapper tests passed, and the CUDA backend library built before the final struct-size tightening. The updated two-GPU regression has not run: the ComputeLab request remained queued and was cancelled.

The focused handle-only compatibility test also passed on ComputeLab after switching to full-size arguments.

display_title: [XLA] Let backends keep converts that would create narrow-float dots

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Let backends keep converts that would create narrow-float dots

ConvertOperandFolding folds value-preserving converts into dots and
convolutions, relying on the folded op accumulating in its result type. That
holds for s8 -> s32 and bf16 -> f32, but not always for 8-bit floats: a dot of
fp8 operands may accumulate with reduced precision (see
ALG_DOT_ANY_F8_ANY_F8_F32_FAST_ACCUM), so folding
dot(convert(f8 -> f32), convert(f8 -> f32)) can change the result of a dot
written in f32 on some hardware.

Add a protected virtual CanFold(instruction, lhs, rhs) that sees a dot or
convolution and the element types it would have after folding. A backend
subclass returns false where it contracts the folded types less precisely. The
default returns true, so the pass behaves as before.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022826081

display_title: Guard RawBufferEntry and PjRtBufferEntry state against concurrent Handle calls.

head_commit.message:
Guard RawBufferEntry and PjRtBufferEntry state against concurrent Handle calls.

`PullTable::Handle` releases the table lock before calling `Entry::Handle`, and
`AwaitPull` replays paused pulls on the registering thread after the entry has
been published. A pull that arrives on the event loop thread at that moment runs
`Entry::Handle` concurrently on the same entry. `RawBufferEntry` and
`PjRtBufferEntry` moved the buffer out of their per-buffer state and updated
`num_consumed_bufs_` without synchronization (`mu_` was declared but never
acquired), so two threads could both take ownership of the same buffer
reference, corrupting its reference count and leading to a use-after-free.
`num_consumed_bufs_` also counted duplicate and out-of-range buffer IDs instead
of distinct consumed buffers.

Both entries now claim each buffer from `arrs_` under `mu_`, immediately fail
duplicate pulls when a buffer has already been claimed, and batch-update
`num_consumed_bufs_` under `mu_` at the end of `Handle` so that only one call
returns `true` once all buffers have been claimed. `mu_` is not held while
registering readiness callbacks or sending errors, since callbacks may schedule
copies and sends inline. Document the concurrency and completion contract on
`PullTable::Entry::Handle` and add regression tests covering concurrent pulls
and duplicate/out-of-range buffer IDs for both entry types.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023508846

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Let backends keep converts that would create narrow-float dots

ConvertOperandFolding folds value-preserving converts into dots and
convolutions, relying on the folded op accumulating in its result type. That
holds for s8 -> s32 and bf16 -> f32, but not always for 8-bit floats: a dot of
fp8 operands may accumulate with reduced precision (see
ALG_DOT_ANY_F8_ANY_F8_F32_FAST_ACCUM), so folding
dot(convert(f8 -> f32), convert(f8 -> f32)) can change the result of a dot
written in f32 on some hardware.

Add a protected virtual CanFold(lhs, rhs) that sees the element types a dot or
convolution would have after folding. A backend subclass returns false for the
type pairs it contracts less precisely. The default returns true, so the pass
behaves as before.

display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023501931

display_title: PR #52913: Do not default to induction InitStep for non-induction dynamic var

head_commit.message:
PR #52913: Do not default to induction InitStep for non-induction dynamic var

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52913

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR resolves a bug with dynamic slice analysis where, when looking for the InitStep for a variable of a while loop body, the current code would default to the value of the while loop induction variable's InitStep if the variable wasn't found or didn't have the relevant metadata. This is incorrect because the induction vars InitStep could be different from that of the variable that is queried.

This PR resolves this by making it possible to return a `std::nullopt` from this method if there is no such metadata for this variable, and if that is the case, AnalyzeDynamicSlice will return with a `std::nullopt` as correctly documented since the dynamic-slice index variable doesn't have any metadata about how it is iterating.

Additionally, this PR adds a check in the HLO verifier that enforces that the while loop and induction variable metadata are consistent and complete if provided.

🎯 Justification
This PR is important to resolve a bug where a dynamic slice index variable gets incorrectly assigned the wrong init-step, and as a result, the execution of the loop indexes the wrong memory regions at the wrong points in the program, leading to incorrect values or NaNs.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No benchmarks as no perf improvements.

🧪 Unit Tests:
Unit tests were added to validate that the dynamic variables with partial or no information are not analyzed (and don't default to the loop induction variables) as well as tests to validate that behavior for staggered variables has not changed.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No new execution tests were added as no new optimizations were implemented.

display_title: Guard RawBufferEntry and PjRtBufferEntry state against concurrent Handle calls.

head_commit.message:
Guard RawBufferEntry and PjRtBufferEntry state against concurrent Handle calls.

`PullTable::Handle` releases the table lock before calling `Entry::Handle`, and
`AwaitPull` replays paused pulls on the registering thread after the entry has
been published. A pull that arrives on the event loop thread at that moment runs
`Entry::Handle` concurrently on the same entry. `RawBufferEntry` and
`PjRtBufferEntry` moved the buffer out of their per-buffer state and updated
`num_consumed_bufs_` without synchronization (`mu_` was declared but never
acquired), so two threads could both take ownership of the same buffer
reference, corrupting its reference count and leading to a use-after-free.
`num_consumed_bufs_` also counted duplicate and out-of-range buffer IDs instead
of distinct consumed buffers.

Both entries now claim each buffer from `arrs_` under `mu_`, immediately fail
duplicate pulls when a buffer has already been claimed, and batch-update
`num_consumed_bufs_` under `mu_` at the end of `Handle` so that only one call
returns `true` once all buffers have been claimed. `mu_` is not held while
registering readiness callbacks or sending errors, since callbacks may schedule
copies and sends inline. Document the concurrency and completion contract on
`PullTable::Entry::Handle` and add regression tests covering concurrent pulls
and duplicate/out-of-range buffer IDs for both entry types.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Snapshot ThunkMetadata and nested CommandBuffer thunks in ProgressTracker

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Snapshot ThunkMetadata and nested CommandBuffer thunks in ProgressTracker

Previously, `ThunkExecutor::ScopedProgressTracker` owned `ProgressTracker` via `std::unique_ptr`, and `ProgressTracker` stored raw `const Thunk*` pointers in `ThunkExecutionEvent` to read `thunk->kind()` and `thunk->profile_annotation()` when formatting progress dumps. If `ProgressTracker` outlives host dispatch to track in-flight device execution, destroying `GpuExecutable` before device execution finishes would leave dangling `const Thunk*` pointers. In addition, when a `CommandBufferThunk` was pending, `ProgressTracker` only recorded the outer `kCommandBuffer` thunk without its nested HLO thunks.

This change:
1. Converts `ScopedProgressTracker::tracker_` to `std::shared_ptr<ProgressTracker>` so callers can retain `ProgressTracker` until enqueued stream work completes while `ScopedProgressTracker` still manages thread-local installation during `ExecuteOnStream`.
2. Snapshots `ThunkMetadata` (`thunk_idx`, `kind`, `name`, and `nested_thunks` for `kCommandBuffer` thunks) during `InstallProgressTracker` so `ProgressTracker` never dereferences `const Thunk*` pointers after `InstallProgressTracker`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022769146

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use the non-legacy Triton support check in `DotStrengthReduction`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use the non-legacy Triton support check in `DotStrengthReduction`.

`DotStrengthReduction` decides whether to strength-reduce a dot partly based
on whether GemmFusion can handle it. It used `legacy_triton::CanTritonHandleGEMM`
for this, but GemmFusion itself uses `IsTritonSupportedInstruction` from
`support.h`. Switch `DotStrengthReduction` to the same check so both passes
agree.

This can change which dots get strength-reduced, because the two checks
differ: for example, the new check requires exactly one contracting
dimension, and it supports a different set of dot algorithms and types.

This is part of the effort to remove `support_legacy.cc`.

display_title: PR #52913: Do not default to induction InitStep for non-induction dynamic var

head_commit.message:
PR #52913: Do not default to induction InitStep for non-induction dynamic var

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52913

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR resolves a bug with dynamic slice analysis where, when looking for the InitStep for a variable of a while loop body, the current code would default to the value of the while loop induction variable's InitStep if the variable wasn't found or didn't have the relevant metadata. This is incorrect because the induction vars InitStep could be different from that of the variable that is queried.

This PR resolves this by making it possible to return a `std::nullopt` from this method if there is no such metadata for this variable, and if that is the case, AnalyzeDynamicSlice will return with a `std::nullopt` as correctly documented since the dynamic-slice index variable doesn't have any metadata about how it is iterating.

Additionally, this PR adds a check in the HLO verifier that enforces that the while loop and induction variable metadata are consistent and complete if provided.

🎯 Justification
This PR is important to resolve a bug where a dynamic slice index variable gets incorrectly assigned the wrong init-step, and as a result, the execution of the loop indexes the wrong memory regions at the wrong points in the program, leading to incorrect values or NaNs.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No benchmarks as no perf improvements.

🧪 Unit Tests:
Unit tests were added to validate that the dynamic variables with partial or no information are not analyzed (and don't default to the loop induction variables) as well as tests to validate that behavior for staggered variables has not changed.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No new execution tests were added as no new optimizations were implemented.

name: CI
display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018968753

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Snapshot ThunkMetadata and nested CommandBuffer thunks in ProgressTracker

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Snapshot ThunkMetadata and nested CommandBuffer thunks in ProgressTracker

Previously, `ThunkExecutor::ScopedProgressTracker` owned `ProgressTracker` via `std::unique_ptr`, and `ProgressTracker` stored raw `const Thunk*` pointers in `ThunkExecutionEvent` to read `thunk->kind()` and `thunk->profile_annotation()` when formatting progress dumps. If `ProgressTracker` outlives host dispatch to track in-flight device execution, destroying `GpuExecutable` before device execution finishes would leave dangling `const Thunk*` pointers. In addition, when a `CommandBufferThunk` was pending, `ProgressTracker` only recorded the outer `kCommandBuffer` thunk without its nested HLO thunks.

This change:
1. Converts `ScopedProgressTracker::tracker_` to `std::shared_ptr<ProgressTracker>` so callers can retain `ProgressTracker` until enqueued stream work completes while `ScopedProgressTracker` still manages thread-local installation during `ExecuteOnStream`.
2. Snapshots `ThunkMetadata` (`thunk_idx`, `kind`, `name`, and `nested_thunks` for `kCommandBuffer` thunks) during `InstallProgressTracker` so `ProgressTracker` never dereferences `const Thunk*` pointers after `InstallProgressTracker`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022769146

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Dump progress on GPU device execution timeouts

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Dump progress on GPU device execution timeouts

Previously, `--xla_gpu_execution_progress_tracking` only wired its progress dump to the host-side terminate watchdog (`--xla_gpu_execution_terminate_timeout`). When a kernel or collective hung on the device after host dispatch returned (`--xla_gpu_device_execution_terminate_timeout` or `ExecutionTimeoutHandler`), the process aborted without logging completed or pending thunks, and `ScopedProgressTracker` on the host stack was destroyed before in-flight device work finished (returning `EventPool` events while they were still pending on the stream).

This change:
1. Extracts `LogExecutionProgress` and `ReleaseProgressTracker` (serialized across threads by `GetProgressLogMutex()` with `[<device_ordinal>]` prefixes on every line, and logging nested `kCommandBuffer` thunks for pending command buffers).
2. Wires `LogExecutionProgress` (via `std::weak_ptr<ProgressTracker>`) to `HangWatchdog::Abort` for both host and device terminate timeouts as well as `ExecutionTimeoutGuards`.
3. Keeps `ProgressTracker` alive in `main_stream->DoHostCallback` (and on early error paths via `cleanup_progress_tracker`) until enqueued device work completes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022685940

display_title: [XLA] Let backends keep converts that would create narrow-float dots

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add a flag to keep converts that would create narrow-float dots

ConvertOperandFolding folds value-preserving converts into dots and
convolutions, relying on the folded op accumulating in its result type. That
holds for s8 -> s32 and bf16 -> f32, but not always for 8-bit floats: a dot of
fp8 operands may accumulate with reduced precision (see
ALG_DOT_ANY_F8_ANY_F8_F32_FAST_ACCUM), so folding
dot(convert(f8 -> f32), convert(f8 -> f32)) can change the result of a dot
written in f32.

Add --xla_keep_converts_of_narrow_float_dots. When true, a dot or convolution
keeps its converts if folding would leave two operands of at most 8 bits, at
least one of them a float. Other contractions fold as before. Off by default.

[IFRT] Require `shape == shard_shape` when `ConcreteEvenSharding` and `ConcreteEvenShardingSpec` are fully replicated

`Sharding::IsFullyReplicated()` and `ShardingSpec::IsFullyReplicated()` document that a fully replicated sharding has `GetShardShape(shape) == shape`, yet `ConcreteEvenShardingSpec` and `ConcreteEvenSharding` allowed construction and deserialization with `is_fully_replicated = true` and `shape != shard_shape`. name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Dump progress on GPU device execution timeouts

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Dump progress on GPU device execution timeouts

Previously, `--xla_gpu_execution_progress_tracking` only wired its progress dump to the host-side terminate watchdog (`--xla_gpu_execution_terminate_timeout`). When a kernel or collective hung on the device after host dispatch returned (`--xla_gpu_device_execution_terminate_timeout` or `ExecutionTimeoutHandler`), the process aborted without logging completed or pending thunks, and `ScopedProgressTracker` on the host stack was destroyed before in-flight device work finished (returning `EventPool` events while they were still pending on the stream).

This change:
1. Extracts `LogExecutionProgress` and `ReleaseProgressTracker` (serialized across threads by `GetProgressLogMutex()` with `[<device_ordinal>]` prefixes on every line, and logging nested `kCommandBuffer` thunks for pending command buffers).
2. Wires `LogExecutionProgress` (via `std::weak_ptr<ProgressTracker>`) to `HangWatchdog::Abort` for both host and device terminate timeouts as well as `ExecutionTimeoutGuards`.
3. Keeps `ProgressTracker` alive in `main_stream->DoHostCallback` (and on early error paths via `cleanup_progress_tracker`) until enqueued device work completes.

name: CI
display_title: [IFRT] Enforce positive shard and device counts and `Sharding`/`ShardingSpec` count agreement

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Enforce positive shard and device counts and `Sharding`/`ShardingSpec` count agreement

`ShardingSpec` subclasses (`OpaqueShardingSpec`, `ConcreteShardingSpec`, `ConcreteEvenShardingSpec`, and `HloShardingSpec`) accepted zero or negative `num_shards` values—particularly when deserialized via `SerDes`—and `Sharding` deserializers called infallible `Create` factories that `CHECK`-crashed when given an empty `DeviceListProto`. In addition, `ConcreteSharding` constructed its projected `ConcreteShardingSpec` with `num_shards = shard_shapes.size()`, which disagreed with `devices()->size()` (and could be `0`) whenever `devices` contained non-addressable devices.

Enforce `1 <= num_shards <= INT_MAX` across `ShardingSpec` and `1 <= devices()->size() <= INT_MAX` across `Sharding` and `BasicDeviceList`, adding fallible `CreateIfValid` factories used by both `Create` (via `CHECK_OK`) and `SerDes` deserializers so malformed wire protos return `absl::InvalidArgumentError`. Project `ConcreteSharding`'s `ConcreteShardingSpec` with `num_shards = devices->size()` so `sharding->devices()->size() == sharding->sharding_spec()->num_shards()` holds universally, and reject all-shards queries and standalone `ConcreteShardingSpec` serialization when only a subset of shard shapes is addressable.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023443887

name: CI
display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Snapshot ThunkMetadata and nested CommandBuffer thunks in ProgressTracker

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Snapshot ThunkMetadata and nested CommandBuffer thunks in ProgressTracker

Previously, `ThunkExecutor::ScopedProgressTracker` owned `ProgressTracker` via `std::unique_ptr`, and `ProgressTracker` stored raw `const Thunk*` pointers in `ThunkExecutionEvent` to read `thunk->kind()` and `thunk->profile_annotation()` when formatting progress dumps. If `ProgressTracker` outlives host dispatch to track in-flight device execution, destroying `GpuExecutable` before device execution finishes would leave dangling `const Thunk*` pointers. In addition, when a `CommandBufferThunk` was pending, `ProgressTracker` only recorded the outer `kCommandBuffer` thunk without its nested HLO thunks.

This change:
1. Converts `ScopedProgressTracker::tracker_` to `std::shared_ptr<ProgressTracker>` so callers can retain `ProgressTracker` until enqueued stream work completes while `ScopedProgressTracker` still manages thread-local installation during `ExecuteOnStream`.
2. Snapshots `ThunkMetadata` (`thunk_idx`, `kind`, `name`, and `nested_thunks` for `kCommandBuffer` thunks) during `InstallProgressTracker` so `ProgressTracker` never dereferences `const Thunk*` pointers after `InstallProgressTracker`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Replace RAFT select_k max_k threshold with F32/BF16 decision-tree heuristics

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Replace RAFT select_k max_k threshold with F32/BF16 decision-tree heuristics

A fixed `GetRaftSelectKMaxK` threshold cannot capture where `raft::matrix::select_k` outperforms `sort + slice` across `(batch, n, k)` shapes up to `k <= 1024`, because crossover points depend on dtype (`F32` vs. `BF16`), stability (`select_k` vs. U64-packed `select_k`), and GPU architecture (Hopper vs. Blackwell).

- Replaces `GetRaftSelectKMaxK` in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/topk_specializer.cc` with benchmark-trained H100 (used for Hopper and earlier CUDA GPUs) and B200 (used for Blackwell+) decision-tree heuristics up to `k <= 1024` across all four comparison pairs: unstable `F32`, unstable `BF16`, U64-packed stable `F32`, and U64-packed stable `BF16`.
- Adds a default-off `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_raft_u64_radix` flag gating U64 Radix shapes (`k > 129 && (n > 20215 || k > 256)`) in `ShouldRewriteStableTopKToUint64` until 2026-11-28 so the 14-day GPU AOT forward-compatibility window for the U64 segmented radix sort fix can elapse.
- Rejects zero-sized dimensions (`batch == 0 || n == 0 || k == 0`) in `SmallBufferOptimization` before evaluating `k / n` or RAFT heuristics.
- Updates `xla/service/gpu/gpu_compiler_test.cc` and `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/topk_specializer_test.cc` to cover the H100/B200 decision boundaries and U64 Radix flag gating.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Split flag registration in MakeDebugOptionsFlags into smaller stack frames.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Split flag registration in MakeDebugOptionsFlags into smaller stack frames.

**Status quo:** `MakeDebugOptionsFlags` in `xla/debug_options_flags.cc`
registers all ~430 flags in a single function. In unoptimized builds every
`tsl::Flag` temporary gets its own stack slot, so the stack frame grows with
every flag. It has now crossed 200 KB, which breaks toolchains that build with
`-Wframe-larger-than=200000 -Werror`.

**Why:** Any new flag tipped it over the limit; the latest one did. Besides the
build break, a ~200 KB frame is also risky when the flags are first parsed on a
thread with a small stack.

**Design choices:** The `flag_list->push_back(...)` calls are moved, unchanged,
into three immediately invoked `[&] { ... }();` lambdas. Each lambda is its own
function with its own frame (~70 KB each), and only one is live at a time. The
`[&]` capture keeps all existing setter helpers in scope, so no flag definition
changes. The setters already capture `debug_options` by value, so nothing stored
in a `tsl::Flag` refers to the lambdas. Optimized builds may inline the lambdas
again, which is fine since stack slots are reused there.

**Compromises:** The registration body is indented by two more spaces, which
makes the diff large (whitespace and re-wrapped help strings only; no flag
name, default, setter, or help text changed). Pending changes touching this
function will need a rebase.

**Alternatives:** (1) Suppressing `-Wframe-larger-than` for this target hides
a real ~200 KB frame. (2) Rolling back the latest flag addition only defers the
problem to the next flag. (3) Moving the setters into a registrar class with
one member function per chunk avoids reindentation but rewrites ~50 setter
helpers and their uses; more invasive for the same effect.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023382718
