Both `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` carry callee references, `io_aliases`, `donated_input_indices`, and argument/result attribute dictionaries, forcing verifiers and passes to template or branch over both ops and unpack raw `DenseI32ArrayAttr` index pairs.

Introducing `IfrtCallOpInterface` (with `getIoAliasPairs()` returning typed `IoAlias` pairs) alongside shared `GetDonatedOrAliasedInputIndices`, `GetAliasedOutputIndices`, `IsDonatedOperand`, `IsAliasedOperand`, `IsDonatedOrAliasedOperand`, and `IsDonatedOrAliasedByUser` queries in `ifrt_interfaces` unifies call verification, donation checking, call deduplication, dead-code elimination, and metadata population.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Move a copy of while loop state into the loop body

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Keep the slice of a parameter with AUTO layout layout-preserving

A slice or dynamic-slice can change the layout if the sliced array has a
fixed layout, so that a layout required by a consumer is not forced onto
that array. An entry computation parameter with AUTO layout is not fixed:
layout assignment chooses its layout, and the layout required by a consumer
of the slice can be given to the parameter at no cost. Treating it as fixed
made the slice transpose its result instead.

IsSliceOfFixedLayoutOperand returns false for a slice of an entry
computation parameter with AUTO layout, so the slice keeps the layout of
the parameter and the parameter takes the layout the consumer requires.

display_title: [XLA] Simplify and speed up region analysis in copy removal

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify and speed up region analysis in copy removal

Region live range analysis repeatedly queried
`HloOrdering::GetExecutionConstraint` and linearly scanned accumulated control
edges on unordered instruction pairs, causing cubic blowups on high fanout
operands inside conditional branches. It also copied per computation instruction
maps on membership checks and scanned all region pairs after interference was
decided.

Answer same computation ordering queries directly from `HloReachabilityMap`
combined with transitive ancestor bitvectors over tentative control edges, and
cache directed cross computation queries. Store `LiveRangeRegions` as sorted
flat vectors, test smaller computation pairs first, stop scanning once
interference is forced, and add a same computation fast path in
`CallGraph::NearestAncestorsInSameComputation`. Move region analysis internals
into `copy_removal.cc`, replace `Relation` with a three bit ordering mask,
replace the per copy analysis budget in `CopyRemover::TryElideCopy` with
`ElideOptions`, store value nodes in a deque, and unify head and tail merge
checks.

Tests:
- `//xla/service:copy_insertion_test`: covers copy elision with many unordered
  readers, high fanout constant conditionals, transitive control edge cycle
  prevention, and interfering reads.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

Constructing an `xla::ifrt::Shape` deferred negative-dimension checks to `Shape::num_elements()` and permitted dimensions whose total element count overflowed `int64_t` or exceeded what bit-size and byte-size calculations could represent. Callers computing `shape.num_elements() * dtype.bit_size()` or `shape.num_elements() * dtype.byte_size()` could silently wrap signed `int64_t` unless every backend and utility repeated its own checked multiplication.

Add `Shape::Create` to validate non-negative dimensions and that the product of non-zero dimensions fits within `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (`INT64_MAX / 128`, accommodating elements up to 128 bits), returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` on invalid dimensions, and delegate `Shape`'s constructor (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Shape::FromProto` to `Shape::Create`. Enforce the same `Shape::kMaxNumElements` bound in `IfrtArrayType::verify`, `VifrtArrayV1Type::verify`, and `PjRtExecutable` shape conversions, remove `Shape::NumElements()`, drop redundant downstream negative-dimension and byte-size overflow checks, and update IFRT unit tests that constructed `Shape` with negative dimensions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1021496910

display_title: PR #52820: [XLA:GPU] Work around large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

head_commit.message:
PR #52820: [XLA:GPU] Work around large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52820

📝 Summary of Changes
Fixes #48979, a JAX/XLA regression.

Large POSIX-FD CUDA VMM allocations can fail with OUT_OF_MEMORY on WSL
despite sufficient free memory. Try the full allocation first, then retry
eligible WSL failures with backing allocations of at most 1 GiB mapped into
one contiguous address range.

Back contiguous device allocations with 1 GiB physical chunks on WSL
when POSIX-FD handles are enabled and fabric/multicast are unavailable.
This avoids the driver failure for large exportable allocations while
preserving sharing support.

Preserve POSIX-FD exportability for multi-GPU sharing. Other platforms keep
their existing allocation path. Locality-domain allocations, enabled FABRIC
handles, and multicast-capable devices are excluded from chunk retries.

Adds a manual 6 GiB plus padding allocator regression and a two-GPU NCCL
large-buffer registration/transfer test. Both check data around every GiB
boundary; the allocator test also checks POSIX-FD handle properties.

Disabling enable_posix_fd_handle would be a shorter workaround, but would
remove POSIX-FD export needed by cross-process GPU sharing and some NCCL
paths. Keep exportable allocations to preserve multi-GPU support under WSL2.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No perf improvements

🧪 Unit Tests:

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight allocator tests, the 6 GiB regression,
formatting, and error-injection checks pass. Three locality-domain tests
skip for version/hardware requirements. The two-GPU NCCL test compiled but
skipped on this one-GPU host. RDMA-enabled cases were not run.

🧪 Execution Tests:
None
Copybara import of the project:

--
f275b8d7a9cb1f9759df96721d88a31dced53613 by Frederic Bastien <fbastien@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Retry large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

WSL can reject large POSIX-FD VMM allocations with OUT_OF_MEMORY despite
sufficient free memory. Try the full-size allocation first, then retry
with backing chunks of at most 1 GiB on WSL with fabric handles disabled
and multicast unsupported. Exclude locality-domain allocations and map the
chunks into one contiguous virtual address range.

Keep POSIX-FD exportability to preserve multi-GPU support under WSL2.
Disabling enable_posix_fd_handle would be shorter, but removes handles
needed by cross-process GPU sharing and some NCCL paths.

Retain only the original first handle and release later creation
references after mapping. Track the mapped prefix for rollback and keep
the existing deallocation path.

Add a manual 6 GiB plus padding allocator regression and a WSL-only NCCL
regression that registers independent 6 GiB buffers, transfers the full
buffer, and checks both sides of each 1 GiB boundary. Skip the NCCL test
before GPU discovery on other operating systems and retain hardware,
memory, and chunking checks.

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight non-RDMA allocator tests, the manual
6 GiB regression, clang-format 17.0.6, and git diff --check pass. Three
upstream locality tests skip for version or hardware requirements. The
full two-GPU NCCL test skips on this single-GPU machine. Earlier local
two-process probes transferred a 6 GiB chunked source into an independent
256 MiB receiver; write and forced peer-read paths passed. The read probe
refreshed source registration per window and confirmed two-segment
imports at all five boundaries. Distinct-GPU execution remains untested.

--
086dc8783f684df908450b7e3d9e70ef491080a1 by Frederic Bastien <fbastien@nvidia.com>:

Document that a loop is only used for WSL.

--
8f33fe6191c28d8be4f5cf05a85c53a8d7fe0d4e by Frederic Bastien <fbastien@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Clarify WSL retries and generalize the NCCL regression

Make the large-buffer NCCL registration test check allocation, registration,
and full-buffer transfer across supported CUDA hosts without requiring WSL
or a particular physical mapping shape. Remove the unused detection and
mapping dependencies.

Use individual eligibility checks inside the WSL retry path, preserving
original status codes and messages while explaining why retries are not
eligible. Return non-OOM allocation failures directly and explicitly guard
the chunk-mapping loop with IsWsl().

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight allocator tests, the manual 6 GiB
regression, clang-format 17.0.6, and git diff --check pass. Fault injection
confirms original non-OOM errors are returned and neither native Linux nor
failed OS detection triggers chunk retries. Three locality-domain tests skip
for version/hardware requirements. The two-GPU NCCL regression compiles but
skips on this single-GPU host; RDMA-enabled cases were not run.

Merging this change closes #52820

[XLA:GPU] Guard the WSL multicast query by driver version

Require CUDA driver API 12.1 before querying MULTICAST_SUPPORTED in the
large-allocation retry. Older drivers or a failed version query retain the
original allocation error without querying the unsupported attribute.

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, formatting, eight allocator tests, and the
large WSL regression pass. Scoped post-OOM driver-version overrides cover
12.0, 12.1, and query failure, including error propagation and cleanup.

remove POSIX-FD export needed by cross-process GPU sharing and some NCCL
paths. Keep exportable allocations to preserve multi-GPU support under WSL2.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add margin-aware early stopping to autotuner profiling.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add margin-aware early stopping to autotuner profiling.

***Problem:*** GPU autotuning runs multiple timed passes and L2 cache flushes unconditionally on every candidate, wasting compilation time on clearly slower or long-running kernels while a fixed duration cutoff misranks close medium-duration contenders due to first-run post-synchronization clock transients.

***Solution:*** Add competitive margin-aware early stopping in `GpuProfiler::Profile` (configurable via `ProfileOptions::adaptive_early_stopping`) that stops after the first timed run when transient timing error is negligible or a candidate falls outside the statistical contender margin of the fastest validated selectable candidate seen on the same `GpuInputBuffers`, while preserving multi-run averaging for close contenders.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1024219530

name: CI
display_title: [IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

Constructing an `xla::ifrt::Shape` deferred negative-dimension checks to `Shape::num_elements()` and permitted dimensions whose total element count overflowed `int64_t` or exceeded what bit-size and byte-size calculations could represent. Callers computing `shape.num_elements() * dtype.bit_size()` or `shape.num_elements() * dtype.byte_size()` could silently wrap signed `int64_t` unless every backend and utility repeated its own checked multiplication.

Add `Shape::Create` to validate non-negative dimensions and that every prefix product of dimensions fits within `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (`INT64_MAX / 128`, accommodating elements up to 128 bits), returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` on invalid dimensions, and delegate `Shape`'s constructor (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Shape::FromProto` to `Shape::Create`. Enforce the same `Shape::kMaxNumElements` bound in `IfrtArrayType::verify` and `VifrtArrayV1Type::verify`, remove `Shape::NumElements()`, drop redundant downstream negative-dimension and byte-size overflow checks, and update IFRT unit tests that constructed `Shape` with negative dimensions.

display_title: [XLA:PjRt] Raise TransposePlan memcpy threshold from 1 MiB to 64 MiB

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PjRt] Raise TransposePlan memcpy threshold from 1 MiB to 64 MiB

Unchunked `inner_kernel_is_memcpy()` plans in `xla/pjrt/transpose.cc` previously used a 1 MiB (`1 << 20`) per-thread parallelization threshold while non-memcpy transpose plans used 64 MiB (`1 << 26`). When memory-bandwidth-bound 1-D or tiled contiguous copies larger than 1 MiB run via `TransposePlan` alongside concurrent async transfers, fanning each copy out across up to 16 threads adds host CPU contention and thread overhead without reducing aggregate H2D wall time.

Unify `kMinBytesPerThread` for `chunk_contiguity_ == ChunkContiguity::kNone` to 64 MiB (`1 << 26`) regardless of `inner_kernel_is_memcpy()`, matching non-memcpy transpose plans and the 64 MiB `kFastPathMaxBytes` threshold in `xla/pjrt/tiled_linearizer.cc`. Plans with contiguous chunking (`ChunkContiguity::kOutput` / `ChunkContiguity::kInput`) keep `kMinBytesPerThread = 1` so chunked pipelined transfers remain parallelized below 64 MiB.

Testing:
* Added `TransposeTest.MemcpyParallelizationThreshold` in `xla/pjrt/transpose_test.cc` covering 16 MiB, 64 MiB, and 128 MiB 1-D copies (`kNone`) and 16 MiB 2-D tiled copies (`kNone` vs `kOutput`).
* Ran `//xla/pjrt:transpose_test` (all shards pass).
* In a 51-step A/B profile of concurrent async H2D transfers on a multi-host TPU training workload, this cut host thread-summed `Transpose::ExecuteChunk` time by 33% (224.9 → 150.0 ms/step), cut host thread count in the trace by 35% (642 → 416), and kept H2D wall-clock union span flat (13.38 → 13.27 ms/step).

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Demote BF16-exact F32 dots to BF16 x BF16 dots.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Demote BF16-exact F32 dots to BF16 x BF16 dots.

***Problem:*** TF32-eligible `dot(convert<f32>(s8), convert<f32>(bf16))` dots run as F32 x F32 GEMMs whose 4-byte operand tiles double register and shared-memory pressure, causing register spills and low memory bandwidth even though every operand value is exactly representable in BF16.

***Solution:*** Extend `DotOperandConverter` to rewrite F32 x F32 dots whose operands are BF16-exact upcasts or reduce-precisions into BF16 x BF16 dots with the same output type, only when the dot already permits TF32 inputs (no explicit algorithm, operand precision at most HIGH, TF32 enabled), so products and F32 accumulation are unchanged.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1024173292

display_title: [IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

Constructing an `xla::ifrt::Shape` deferred negative-dimension checks to `Shape::num_elements()` and permitted dimensions whose total element count overflowed `int64_t` or exceeded what bit-size and byte-size calculations could represent. Callers computing `shape.num_elements() * dtype.bit_size()` or `shape.num_elements() * dtype.byte_size()` could silently wrap signed `int64_t` unless every backend and utility repeated its own checked multiplication.

Add `Shape::Create` to validate non-negative dimensions and that every prefix product of dimensions fits within `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (`INT64_MAX / 128`, accommodating elements up to 128 bits), returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` on invalid dimensions, and delegate `Shape`'s constructor (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Shape::FromProto` to `Shape::Create`. Remove `Shape::NumElements()`, drop redundant downstream negative-dimension and byte-size overflow checks, and update IFRT unit tests that constructed `Shape` with negative dimensions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1021496910

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Simplify and speed up region analysis in copy removal

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify and speed up region analysis in copy removal

Region live range analysis repeatedly queried
`HloOrdering::GetExecutionConstraint` and linearly scanned accumulated control
edges on unordered instruction pairs, causing cubic blowups on high fanout
operands inside conditional branches. It also copied per computation instruction
maps on membership checks and scanned all region pairs after interference was
decided.

Answer same computation ordering queries directly from `HloReachabilityMap`
combined with transitive ancestor bitvectors over tentative control edges, and
cache directed cross computation queries. Store `LiveRangeRegions` as sorted
flat vectors, test smaller computation pairs first, stop scanning once
interference is forced, and add a same computation fast path in
`CallGraph::NearestAncestorsInSameComputation`. Move region analysis internals
into `copy_removal.cc`, replace `Relation` with a three bit ordering mask,
replace the per copy analysis budget in `CopyRemover::TryElideCopy` with
`ElideOptions`, store value nodes in a deque, and unify head and tail merge
checks.

Tests:
- `//xla/service:copy_insertion_test`: covers copy elision with many unordered
  readers, high fanout constant conditionals, transitive control edge cycle
  prevention, and interfering reads.

display_title: [XLA:PjRt] Raise TransposePlan memcpy threshold from 1 MiB to 64 MiB

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PjRt] Raise TransposePlan memcpy threshold from 1 MiB to 64 MiB

Unchunked `inner_kernel_is_memcpy()` plans in `xla/pjrt/transpose.cc` previously used a 1 MiB (`1 << 20`) per-thread parallelization threshold while non-memcpy transpose plans used 64 MiB (`1 << 26`). When memory-bandwidth-bound 1-D or tiled contiguous copies larger than 1 MiB run via `TransposePlan` alongside concurrent async transfers, fanning each copy out across up to 16 threads adds host CPU contention and thread overhead without reducing aggregate H2D wall time.

Unify `kMinBytesPerThread` for `chunk_contiguity_ == ChunkContiguity::kNone` to 64 MiB (`1 << 26`) regardless of `inner_kernel_is_memcpy()`, matching non-memcpy transpose plans and the 64 MiB `kFastPathMaxBytes` threshold in `xla/pjrt/tiled_linearizer.cc`. Plans with contiguous chunking (`ChunkContiguity::kOutput` / `ChunkContiguity::kInput`) keep `kMinBytesPerThread = 1` so chunked pipelined transfers remain parallelized below 64 MiB.

Testing:
* Added `TransposeTest.MemcpyParallelizationThreshold` in `xla/pjrt/transpose_test.cc` covering 16 MiB, 64 MiB, and 128 MiB 1-D copies (`kNone`) and 16 MiB 2-D tiled copies (`kNone` vs `kOutput`).
* Ran `//xla/pjrt:transpose_test` (all shards pass).
* In a 51-step A/B profile of concurrent async H2D transfers on a multi-host TPU training workload, this cut host thread-summed `Transpose::ExecuteChunk` time by 33% (224.9 → 150.0 ms/step), cut host thread count in the trace by 35% (642 → 416), and kept H2D wall-clock union span flat (13.38 → 13.27 ms/step).
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1024115881

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Replace RAFT select_k max_k threshold with F32/BF16 decision-tree heuristics

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Replace RAFT select_k max_k threshold with F32/BF16 decision-tree heuristics

A fixed `GetRaftSelectKMaxK` threshold cannot capture where `raft::matrix::select_k` outperforms `sort + slice` across `(batch, n, k)` shapes up to `k <= 1024`, because crossover points depend on dtype (`F32` vs. `BF16`), stability (`select_k` vs. U64-packed `select_k`), and GPU architecture (Hopper vs. Blackwell).

- Replaces `GetRaftSelectKMaxK` in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/topk_specializer.cc` with benchmark-trained H100 (used for Hopper and earlier CUDA GPUs) and B200 (used for Blackwell+) decision-tree heuristics up to `k <= 1024` across all four comparison pairs: unstable `F32`, unstable `BF16`, U64-packed stable `F32`, and U64-packed stable `BF16`.
- Adds a default-off `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_raft_u64_radix` flag gating U64 Radix shapes (`k > 129 && (n > 20215 || k > 256)`) in `ShouldRewriteStableTopKToUint64` until 2026-11-28 so the 14-day GPU AOT forward-compatibility window for the U64 segmented radix sort fix can elapse.
- Rejects zero-sized dimensions (`batch == 0 || n == 0 || k == 0`) in `SmallBufferOptimization` before evaluating `k / n` or RAFT heuristics.
- Updates `xla/service/gpu/gpu_compiler_test.cc` and `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/topk_specializer_test.cc` to cover the H100/B200 decision boundaries and U64 Radix flag gating.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1024144726

display_title: [XLA:PjRt] Raise TransposePlan memcpy threshold from 1 MiB to 64 MiB

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PjRt] Raise TransposePlan memcpy threshold from 1 MiB to 64 MiB

Unchunked `inner_kernel_is_memcpy()` plans in `xla/pjrt/transpose.cc` previously used a 1 MiB (`1 << 20`) per-thread parallelization threshold while non-memcpy transpose plans used 64 MiB (`1 << 26`). When memory-bandwidth-bound 1-D or tiled contiguous copies larger than 1 MiB run via `TransposePlan` alongside concurrent async transfers, fanning each copy out across up to 16 threads adds host CPU contention and thread overhead without reducing aggregate H2D wall time.

Unify `kMinBytesPerThread` for `chunk_contiguity_ == ChunkContiguity::kNone` to 64 MiB (`1 << 26`) regardless of `inner_kernel_is_memcpy()`, matching non-memcpy transpose plans and the 64 MiB `kFastPathMaxBytes` threshold in `xla/pjrt/tiled_linearizer.cc`. Plans with contiguous chunking (`ChunkContiguity::kOutput` / `ChunkContiguity::kInput`) keep `kMinBytesPerThread = 1` so chunked pipelined transfers remain parallelized below 64 MiB.

Testing:
* Added `TransposeTest.MemcpyParallelizationThreshold` in `xla/pjrt/transpose_test.cc` covering 16 MiB, 64 MiB, and 128 MiB 1-D copies (`kNone`) and 16 MiB 2-D tiled copies (`kNone` vs `kOutput`).
* Ran `//xla/pjrt:transpose_test` (all shards pass).
* In a 51-step A/B profile of concurrent async H2D transfers on a multi-host TPU training workload, this cut host thread-summed `Transpose::ExecuteChunk` time by 33% (224.9 → 150.0 ms/step), cut host thread count in the trace by 35% (642 → 416), and kept H2D wall-clock union span flat (13.38 → 13.27 ms/step).
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1024115881

display_title: [XLA] Simplify and speed up region analysis in copy removal

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify and speed up region analysis in copy removal

Region live range analysis repeatedly queried
`HloOrdering::GetExecutionConstraint` and linearly scanned accumulated control
edges on unordered instruction pairs, causing cubic blowups on high fanout
operands inside conditional branches. It also copied per computation instruction
maps on membership checks and scanned all region pairs after interference was
decided.

Answer same computation ordering queries directly from `HloReachabilityMap`
combined with transitive ancestor bitvectors over tentative control edges, and
cache directed cross computation queries. Store `LiveRangeRegions` as sorted
flat vectors, test smaller computation pairs first, stop scanning once
interference is forced, and add a same computation fast path in
`CallGraph::NearestAncestorsInSameComputation`. Move region analysis internals
into `copy_removal.cc`, replace `Relation` with a three bit ordering mask,
replace the per copy analysis budget in `CopyRemover::TryElideCopy` with
`ElideOptions`, store value nodes in a deque, and unify head and tail merge
checks.

Tests:
- `//xla/service:copy_insertion_test`: covers copy elision with many unordered
  readers, high fanout constant conditionals, transitive control edge cycle
  prevention, and interfering reads.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022988184

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Replace RAFT select_k max_k threshold with F32/BF16 decision-tree heuristics

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Replace RAFT select_k max_k threshold with F32/BF16 decision-tree heuristics

A fixed `GetRaftSelectKMaxK` threshold cannot capture where `raft::matrix::select_k` outperforms `sort + slice` across `(batch, n, k)` shapes up to `k <= 1024`, because crossover points depend on dtype (`F32` vs. `BF16`), stability (`select_k` vs. U64-packed `select_k`), and GPU architecture (Hopper vs. Blackwell).

- Replaces `GetRaftSelectKMaxK` in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/topk_specializer.cc` with benchmark-trained H100 (used for Hopper and earlier CUDA GPUs) and B200 (used for Blackwell+) decision-tree heuristics up to `k <= 1024` across all four comparison pairs: unstable `F32`, unstable `BF16`, U64-packed stable `F32`, and U64-packed stable `BF16`.
- Adds a default-off `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_raft_u64_radix` flag gating U64 Radix shapes (`k > 129 && (n > 20215 || k > 256)`) in `ShouldRewriteStableTopKToUint64` until 2026-11-28 so the 14-day GPU AOT forward-compatibility window for the U64 segmented radix sort fix can elapse.
- Rejects zero-sized dimensions (`batch == 0 || n == 0 || k == 0`) in `SmallBufferOptimization` before evaluating `k / n` or RAFT heuristics.
- Updates `xla/service/gpu/gpu_compiler_test.cc` and `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/topk_specializer_test.cc` to cover the H100/B200 decision boundaries and U64 Radix flag gating.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015255316

display_title: [IFRT IR] Add outlined atom-program module helpers in IFRT IR

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Add outlined atom-program module helpers in IFRT IR

Outlining and compilation passes in IFRT IR each manually resolve `@module::@main` atom-program callees, construct nested `@module::@callee` symbol references, and clone private nested `ModuleOp`s into the root symbol table. Repeating this plumbing across `IfrtOutlineAtomProgramToModulePass`, `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass`, and `IfrtLowerMpmdReshardToCallPass` scatters identical module-hierarchy checks and symbol-visibility boilerplate across passes.

Adding `MakeOutlinedCalleeSymbolRef`, `GetCalleeRootSymbolOp`, `GetOutlinedAtomProgramModule`, and `CloneOutlinedAtomProgramModule` in `ifrt/ir/utils` provides shared primitives for resolving and privately cloning one-level outlined atom-program modules, allowing those outlining and compilation passes to drop their local module-lookup and cloning helpers.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1024108772

display_title: [Mosaic-SC] Support unaligned offset vector lengths in indirect DMAs

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic-SC] Support unaligned offset vector lengths in indirect DMAs

Relax the `tpu.enqueue_indirect_dma` verifier contract for 1D vector
`offsets` so the local memref's leading dimension defines an active prefix in
`[1, num_offsets]`, rather than matching `num_offsets` exactly. Trailing
offsets beyond the local memref's leading dimension are ignored, and
`wait_indirect_dma` counts bytes from the local memref.

Also guard against unsigned underflow in `verifyGather` and `verifyScatter`
when the local memref rank is smaller than `offsets_rank`, update
`xla/mosaic/dialect/tpu/tpu_ops.td` documentation, and mirror the verification
tests in `xla/mosaic/dialect/tpu/tpu_ops_verification_test.cc`.

display_title: [XLA] Keep diagonal scale factored out of InvertDiagonalBlocks

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Keep diagonal scale factored out of InvertDiagonalBlocks

`TriangularSolveExpander::InvertDiagonalBlocks` previously materialized
`A_jj^{-1} = U^{-1} D^{-1}` by dividing out `D = diag(A_jj)` at the end of
block inversion. For normal inputs with large magnitude (e.g. `2^123`),
off-diagonal entries of `A_jj^{-1}` fell below `FLT_MIN` and flushed to zero on
FTZ targets; for small inputs (e.g. `2^-123` in `F32` or `2^-14` in `F16`),
off-diagonal entries overflowed to infinity even when the true solution was
`O(1)`.

Keep `D = diag(A_jj)` factored out using row-scaling `A_jj = D U`:

- Change `TriangularSolveExpander::InvertDiagonalBlocks` to row-normalize
  `U = D^{-1} A_jj` (using `GetMatrixDiagonalViaGather` and explicitly masking
  the diagonal to `1.0` and the ignored triangle to `0.0` to avoid `Inf / Inf`
  and `0 / 0` `NaN`s) and return `U^{-1} = A_jj^{-1} D`.
- In `SolveWithInvertedDiagonalBlocks`, when `!unit_diagonal`, gather `diag(a)`
  once via `GetMatrixDiagonalViaGather` and apply `D^{-1}` directly to the
  remainder or block output according to `(left_side, transpose_a,
  conjugate_a)`.

This cancels extreme scales per-row and per-batch without global reductions,
covers all float and complex types (`F16`, `BF16`, `F32`, `F64`, `C64`,
`C128`), and preserves subnormals on non-FTZ targets.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022890370

display_title: [IFRT IR] Add outlined atom-program module helpers in IFRT IR

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Add outlined atom-program module helpers in IFRT IR

Outlining and compilation passes in IFRT IR each manually resolve `@module::@main` atom-program callees, construct nested `@module::@callee` symbol references, and clone private nested `ModuleOp`s into the root symbol table. Repeating this plumbing across `IfrtOutlineAtomProgramToModulePass`, `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass`, and `IfrtLowerMpmdReshardToCallPass` scatters identical module-hierarchy checks and symbol-visibility boilerplate across passes.

Adding `MakeOutlinedCalleeSymbolRef`, `GetCalleeRootSymbolOp`, `GetOutlinedAtomProgramModule`, and `CloneOutlinedAtomProgramModule` in `ifrt/ir/utils` provides shared primitives for resolving and privately cloning one-level outlined atom-program modules, allowing those outlining and compilation passes to drop their local module-lookup and cloning helpers.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Replace RAFT select_k max_k threshold with F32/BF16 decision-tree heuristics

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Replace RAFT select_k max_k threshold with F32/BF16 decision-tree heuristics

A fixed `GetRaftSelectKMaxK` threshold cannot capture where `raft::matrix::select_k` outperforms `sort + slice` across `(batch, n, k)` shapes up to `k <= 1024`, because crossover points depend on dtype (`F32` vs. `BF16`), stability (`select_k` vs. U64-packed `select_k`), and GPU architecture (Hopper vs. Blackwell).

- Replaces `GetRaftSelectKMaxK` in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/topk_specializer.cc` with benchmark-trained H100 (used for Hopper and earlier CUDA GPUs) and B200 (used for Blackwell+) decision-tree heuristics up to `k <= 1024` across all four comparison pairs: unstable `F32`, unstable `BF16`, U64-packed stable `F32`, and U64-packed stable `BF16`.
- Adds a default-off `--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_raft_u64_radix` flag gating U64 Radix shapes (`k > 129 && (n > 20215 || k > 256)`) in `ShouldRewriteStableTopKToUint64` until 2026-11-28 so the 14-day GPU AOT forward-compatibility window for the U64 segmented radix sort fix can elapse.
- Rejects zero-sized dimensions (`batch == 0 || n == 0 || k == 0`) in `SmallBufferOptimization` before evaluating `k / n` or RAFT heuristics.
- Updates `xla/service/gpu/gpu_compiler_test.cc` and `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/topk_specializer_test.cc` to cover the H100/B200 decision boundaries and U64 Radix flag gating.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015255316

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Align permuted contracting shardings in windowed dot

In `dot_handler.cc`, reduce scatter windowed einsum in `EmitWindowedDotGeneral` and `GetWindowedEinsumConfiguration` gated contracting operand alignment on `RequiresTransposeSharding`, which checks only whether per dimension shard counts differ. When `lhs` and `rhs` have equal contracting shard counts with different device orders across mesh axes, resharding was skipped and partitions contracted mismatched shards. Check `lhs.sharding() != *rhs_sharding_transposed_to_match_lhs` when `operands_sharded_at_contracting_dims` is true, and check `lhs_sharding != *rhs_sharding_transposed_to_match_lhs` in the cost estimate so permuted contracting shardings reshard before the loop.

display_title: [SDY] Add need replication sharding rule for TopKBatchMajorSmallK

head_commit.message:
[SDY] Add need replication sharding rule for TopKBatchMajorSmallK

In `CustomCallShardingRuleOpInterface::getShardingRule`, custom call target `@TopK` registers an `OpShardingRuleAttr`, whereas `@TopKBatchMajorSmallK` had no sharding rule entry and returned an empty attribute. During Shardy global to local partitioning, `InsertExplicitReshardsPass` skips operations without a rule and `ConvertGlobalToLocalPass` localizes sharded operands without an `all_gather`, producing wrong local results. Register a sharding rule for validated static rank two `@TopKBatchMajorSmallK` calls with matching batch sizes that marks all dimensions with `FactorType::kNeedReplication` and blocked propagation.

[XLA:SPMD] Reshard block-scaled dot scales to match operand shardings

`PartitionedHloMX` requires its data operand and scale factor to have identical
shardings (`CHECK_EQ(operand.sharding(), scale.sharding())`). When partitioning
a `__op$block_scaled_dot` custom call whose operand and scale have different
shardings (such as a sharded operand paired with a replicated scale),
`SpmdPartitioningVisitor::HandleDotHelper` previously crashed on that check.

Reshard `lhs_scale` and `rhs_scale` to `lhs_operand.sharding()` and
`rhs_operand.sharding()`, respectively, before constructing `PartitionedHloMX`.
When the operand and scale already share the same sharding,
`PartitionedHlo::Reshard` is a no-op.

The sharded block-scaled dot infers the block size from the shard shapes, so
each shard along the contracting dimension must hold a whole number of blocks.
If an operand's contracting shard count does not divide both the `lhs_scale`
and `rhs_scale` contracting sizes (checked against both, since `PartitionDot`
may reshard one operand to the other's contracting sharding), replicate the
contracting dimension of that operand first.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/49386

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Assign async D2D copies to a single dedicated stream.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Assign async D2D copies to a single dedicated stream.

***Problem:*** Asynchronous device-to-device copy-start instructions and dynamic-slice copy fusions fall back to the general compute stream pool, round-robining device-to-device memory copies across multiple compute streams and contending with asynchronous compute kernels.

***Solution:*** Classify unannotated device-to-device copy-start and dynamic-slice copy fusion-start scopes as kMemcpyD2D when dedicated memcpy streams are enabled and assign them to a single shared ComputationStreamId disjoint from active compute streams.

display_title: [XLA] Check root tuple increment in WhileUtil::IncrementWhileLoopTripCount

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check root tuple increment in WhileUtil::IncrementWhileLoopTripCount

WhileUtil::IncrementWhileLoopTripCount previously accepted any while loop body
where some user of the induction variable tuple element added 1, even when the
loop body root updated the induction variable by a larger step such as 2, and
used logical AND instead of logical OR when validating the condition tuple
element. Check the loop body root tuple or aliased custom call root element
directly for an increment of 1 on the loop parameter tuple element and use
logical OR for the condition check so non unit stride loops are rejected
cleanly.

head_commit.message:
[SDY] Add need replication sharding rule for TopKBatchMajorSmallK

In `CustomCallShardingRuleOpInterface::getShardingRule`, custom call target `@TopK` registers an `OpShardingRuleAttr`, whereas `@TopKBatchMajorSmallK` had no sharding rule entry and returned an empty attribute. During Shardy global to local partitioning, `InsertExplicitReshardsPass` skips operations without a rule and `ConvertGlobalToLocalPass` localizes sharded operands without an `all_gather`, producing wrong local results. Register a sharding rule for validated static rank two `@TopKBatchMajorSmallK` calls with matching batch sizes that marks all dimensions with `FactorType::kNeedReplication` and blocked propagation.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Treat Triton collective fusions as async collectives.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Treat Triton collective fusions as async collectives.

***Problem:*** Asynchronous __triton_collective custom fusions wrapped in fusion-start and fusion-done are classified as generic compute scopes instead of collective communications, spreading device-barrier collectives across multiple compute streams, bypassing collective overlap limits in the latency-hiding scheduler, and leaving unoverlapped pairs asynchronous.

***Solution:*** Unwrap __triton_collective fusions to their inner collective hero across execution stream assignment, latency-hiding scheduling, collective domain legalization, sync-collective annotation, and async-to-sync conversion while preserving the outer fusion backend config.

display_title: PR #52240: [XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in dot rewriters

head_commit.message:
PR #52240: [XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in dot rewriters

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52240

:pencil: **Summary of Changes**

Preserve frontend attributes when dot rewriters replace a dot with new instructions. New dots are added with `HloInstruction::AddInstruction` on the original dot, which derives them via `SetupDerivedInstruction` (also carrying metadata and, where shapes allow, sharding, like existing rewriters such as `DotDimensionSorter`), so they inherit the original dot's frontend attributes instead of silently dropping them. This covers `DotAlgorithmRewriter` (the BF16/TF32 decompositions in `backends/gpu/transforms` and the FP8xN decomposition in `hlo/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter.cc`), `ScaledDotRewriter`, `SplitkRewriter`, and `GemmFusionSwapOperands`.

:dart: **Justification**

Frontend attributes are the mechanism by which the frontend (e.g. JAX) attaches annotations to HLO instructions for downstream passes to consume. When a pass replaces an instruction, it must carry those attributes over to the replacement; otherwise the annotation is silently dropped and the consumers that depend on it no longer see it. These dot rewriters were not doing this, so annotated matmuls lost their scheduling annotations.

:compass: **Design: deriving replacements from the original dot**

Each new dot is added with `original_dot->AddInstruction(...)`, which derives it via `SetupDerivedInstruction` (metadata, frontend attributes, and sharding where the shapes allow). Instructions built by helpers call `SetupDerivedInstruction` directly: the instruction that replaces the dot in `RewriteDotWithOperandPairs` (shared by BF16X3/X6/X9 and TF32X3) and `RewriteFp8xNDot` (FP8X3/X4), and the split-K dot, which `MakeDotHlo` creates. So every new dot and the instruction that replaces the original keep the annotation.

:rocket: **Kind of Contribution**

:bug: Bug Fix

:test_tube: **Unit Tests:**

Added hardware-independent tests asserting frontend attributes survive each dot rewrite:

* `backends/gpu/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `KeepsFrontendAttributes`, parameterized over every `PrecisionConfig::Algorithm`: verifies that after the pass every dot and the instruction that replaces the dot keep the attributes. Without the fix it fails for the seven algorithms the pass decomposes (BF16, BF16X3/X6/X9, TF32X3, FP8X3/X4); new algorithms are covered automatically.
* `hlo/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `RewriteFp8xNDotStructureTest.KeepsFrontendAttributes`, for FP8X3 and FP8X4 at both precisions: verifies every F8 dot and the instruction that replaces the dot keep them.
* `gemm_fusion_swap_operands_test.cc`:
  * `SwappedDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the swapped dot keeps them.
* `scaled_dot_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `RewrittenDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the dot replacing a scaled-dot keeps them.
* `splitk_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `SplitKDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the split-K dot keeps them.

:test_tube: **Execution Tests:**

No new checked-in execution test was added.

display_title: [XLA:SDY] Support JAX custom_partitioning in Shardy partitioner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SDY] Support JAX custom_partitioning in Shardy partitioner

When the Shardy partitioner is fully enabled, GSPMD is completely bypassed,
leaving `stablehlo.custom_call @CustomSPMDPartitioning` unpartitioned and
failing compilation. To support it, we change the following:

- **Partitioner-agnostic callback API**: Add `CustomCallPartitioner::PartitionToMlir`
  (defaulting to `std::nullopt` for GSPMD-only C++ partitioners) and share PJRT
  C-API callback marshaling in `CApiCustomCallPartitioner` between GSPMD and
  Shardy.

- **Callback MLIR preparation**: Upgrade VHLO, inline direct helper calls, and
  legalize CHLO and complex math on the shard-local module returned by the
  callback, remapping positive `channel_handle` IDs via `nextChannelId` and
  importing remaining private helpers (such as `stablehlo.composite`
  decompositions) into `symbolTable`.

- **Global-IR lowering (`resolvePermutationFactors`)**: Wire
  `custom_spmd_partitioning.{h,cc}` into `CustomCallPartitioningOpInterface`,
  rewriting custom-partitioned calls into operand `sdy.reshard` +
  `sdy.manual_computation` + result `sdy.reshard`.

display_title: Let PJRT GPU client set compute stream priority.

head_commit.message:
Let PJRT GPU client set compute stream priority.

`LocalDeviceState` can create a device's streams at a given priority (`StreamOptions::priority`), and TensorFlow uses that for the priorities of its GPU virtual devices. The PJRT GPU client always creates its `LocalDeviceState` without stream options, so its compute stream always has the default priority.

Add `GpuClientOptions::compute_stream_priority` and pass it on as stream options. When it is set, each device of the client creates its compute stream at that priority. The host-to-device and device-to-host streams get the same priority, and device-to-device streams keep their own fixed priority. If it's unset, the default priority will apply.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023978531

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support native MLIR kInput, multi-output, and DAG stages in MultiPhaseFusion.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support native MLIR kInput, multi-output, and DAG stages in MultiPhaseFusion.

`ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` can now lower `kReduction`, `kTranspose`, and `kConcatenate` sub-kernels with any rank, shared memory reuse, partial-CTA barriers, tuple output unpacking, and arbitrary phase DAGs ordered topologically.

Delegate stage eligibility and launch-dimension queries in `MultiPhaseFusion` to `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion::CreateNativeNestedEmitter` (exempting `kLoop` and `kConcatenate` sub-kernels from the warp-multiple thread guard), wrap unfused instructions using `FusionWrapper::ChooseFusionKind`, unpack/rewire multi-output tuple stages via `get-tuple-element`, and generalize subgraph discovery from straight-line chains to connected DAGs while capping total fused kernel arguments (deduplicated external operands plus leaf outputs) at 256.

PR #50727: [CPU] Flush subnormal inputs in the atan2 builtins

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50727

## Summary

XLA:CPU executes libm calls with flush-to-zero and denormals-are-zero enabled, and glibc's `atan2`/`atan2f` misbehave on subnormal inputs in that state: subnormal pairs can give the wrong quadrant (for example `atan2(2^-1074, 2^-1074)` returns pi/2 instead of the correct result for flushed inputs), and `atan2f(denorm_min, 1)` can return NaN.

This registers guarded `BuiltinAtan2` and `BuiltinAtan2f` CPU builtins that flush subnormal inputs to signed zero before calling libm. A single templated helper inspects the operand bits (floating-point comparisons can already treat subnormals as zero under DAZ), flushes only nonzero subnormals, and preserves each flushed input's sign so quadrant selection still works. Signed zeros, infinities, and NaNs pass through unchanged. The builtins do not read or modify the floating-point environment, so no denormal state is saved, changed, or restored around the libm call.

Fixes tensorflow/tensorflow#129083.

## Kind of contribution

Bug fix and regression tests.

## Tests and validation

- `//xla/backends/cpu/codegen:builtin_atan2_test`:
  - Hardcoded expectations for flushed f64 and f32 subnormal inputs. Once the inputs are zeroed, every case reduces to one of +/-0, +/-pi/2, or +/-pi.
  - A cross-product loop over subnormal, normal, signed-zero, infinity, and NaN operands under all four FTZ/DAZ state combinations checks that the caller's denormal state is left untouched and that non-subnormal inputs pass through unchanged (compared against `std::atan2`/`atan2f` called directly).
  - `GlibcDenormalMisbehaviors` covers the specific wrong-quadrant and NaN cases seen with glibc.
- `//xla/tests:atan2_test`: new `F64SubnormalOperands` and `F32SubnormalOperands` cases with hardcoded expected results. They use runtime parameters so the subnormal inputs reach compiled code instead of being constant-folded, and they are guarded to CPU only (`test::DeviceTypeIs(test::kCpu)`) because GPU does not zero subnormals and returns pi/4 for `atan2(tiny, tiny)`.
- The issue was reproduced on Linux x86-64 emulation with the reported `tf-nightly==2.23.0.dev20261011`, with the original input bits preserved, and confirmed in a direct libm probe with FTZ/DAZ enabled.
- In this update, `builtin_atan2.cc` was also compiled and run standalone to check the templated helper (flushed pair gives +0, opposite signs give pi, a normal operand against a flushed one gives pi/2, and the f32 case is not NaN). A full local Bazel run of the updated tests was not possible in the current environment (the local Bazel server cannot start), so those results are pending CI.

## Performance

The normal-input path only adds bit inspection of the two operands before the libm call; there is no floating-point state change to pay for. No benchmark numbers are claimed for this version.

display_title: [IFRT] Reject unsupported `xla::HloSharding` kinds in `HloSharding` and `HloShardingSpec`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Reject unsupported `xla::HloSharding` kinds in `HloSharding` and `HloShardingSpec`

`xla::ifrt::HloSharding` and `xla::ifrt::HloShardingSpec` model leaf array shardings, yet accepted compiler-internal `Tuple`, `Unknown`, and `ShardGroup` `xla::HloSharding` instances during construction and `SerDes` deserialization, which could later `CHECK`-fail inside `TiledDataRank()`, `EachTile()`, or `ToProto()`. In addition, `HloShardingSpecSerDes::Serialize` lacked the `HloShardingV3` guard present in `HloShardingSerDes::Serialize`, neither deserializer rejected `OpSharding` payloads carrying `named_sharding` (which `CHECK`-crash inside `NamedSharding::FromProto` when malformed), and `HloShardingSerDes` inherited from `RTTIExtends<HloSharding, SerDes>` instead of `RTTIExtends<HloShardingSerDes, SerDes>`.

Reject `IsTuple()`, `IsUnknown()`, and `IsShardGroup()` in `HloShardingSpec::CreateIfValid`, remove dead `IsUnknown()` / `!IsTiled()` branches in `HloShardingSpec`, reject `HloShardingV3` (`named_sharding`) symmetrically in both `HloShardingSerDes` and `HloShardingSpecSerDes` serialization and deserialization, and fix `HloShardingSerDes`'s RTTI base class.

display_title: Let PJRT GPU client set compute stream priority.

head_commit.message:
Let PJRT GPU client set compute stream priority.

`LocalDeviceState` can create a device's streams at a given priority (`StreamOptions::priority`), and TensorFlow uses that for the priorities of its GPU virtual devices. The PJRT GPU client always creates its `LocalDeviceState` without stream options, so its compute stream always has the default priority.

Add `GpuClientOptions::compute_stream_priority` and pass it on as stream options. When it is set, each device of the client creates its compute stream at that priority. The host-to-device and device-to-host streams get the same priority, and device-to-device streams keep their own fixed priority. If it's unset, the default priority will apply.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Do not force async interception past the end of a live range

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Do not force async interception past the end of a live range

Region live range analysis unconditionally flagged every asynchronous start, asynchronous done, and collective permute instruction as intercepting every def/use pair in the compared buffer. When an async consumer ran strictly after a conditional passthrough branch or in a mutually exclusive branch, that forced flag rejected safe buffer sharing and kept large copies alive.

Only force interception when the instruction is not strictly after the use and is not in a mutually exclusive branch. Existing programs elide redundant copies feeding postconditional async operations without changing numerical behavior.

Tests:
- `//xla/service:copy_insertion_test`: verifies copy elision when a conditional passthrough branch feeds an `async-start` and `async-done` pair.

display_title: [XLA] Do not force async interception past the end of a live range

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Do not force async interception past the end of a live range

Region live range analysis unconditionally flagged every asynchronous start, asynchronous done, and collective permute instruction as intercepting every def/use pair in the compared buffer. When an async consumer ran strictly after a conditional passthrough branch or in a mutually exclusive branch, that forced flag rejected safe buffer sharing and kept large copies alive.

Only force interception when the instruction is not strictly after the use and is not in a mutually exclusive branch. Existing programs elide redundant copies feeding postconditional async operations without changing numerical behavior.

Tests:
- `//xla/service:copy_insertion_test`: verifies copy elision when a conditional passthrough branch feeds an `async-start` and `async-done` pair.

display_title: [IFRT] Require `shape == shard_shape` when `ConcreteEvenSharding` and `ConcreteEvenShardingSpec` are fully replicated

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Require `shape == shard_shape` when `ConcreteEvenSharding` and `ConcreteEvenShardingSpec` are fully replicated

`Sharding::IsFullyReplicated()` and `ShardingSpec::IsFullyReplicated()` document that a fully replicated sharding has `GetShardShape(shape) == shape`, yet `ConcreteEvenShardingSpec` and `ConcreteEvenSharding` allowed construction and deserialization with `is_fully_replicated = true` and `shape != shard_shape`. Downstream methods (`IndexDomains`, `UniqueIndexDomains`, `ShardToUniqueIndexDomainIndex`) had to carry extra `this->shape() == shard_shape()` guards to work around contradictory instances.

Reject `is_fully_replicated == true` when `shape != shard_shape` in `ConcreteEvenShardingSpec::CreateIfValid` (covering `Create` and `SerDes` for both `ConcreteEvenShardingSpec` and `ConcreteEvenSharding`), drop the redundant `this->shape() == shard_shape()` checks, and update unit tests in `sharding_test`, `sharding_spec_test`, `sharding_serdes_test`, and `basic_string_array_test` that constructed `ConcreteEvenSharding` with `is_fully_replicated = true` and `shape != shard_shape`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023880275

display_title: [IFRT IR] Add outlined atom-program module helpers in IFRT IR

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Add outlined atom-program module helpers in IFRT IR

Outlining and compilation passes in IFRT IR each manually resolve `@module::@main` atom-program callees, construct nested `@module::@callee` symbol references, and clone private nested `ModuleOp`s into the root symbol table. Repeating this plumbing across `IfrtOutlineAtomProgramToModulePass`, `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass`, and `IfrtLowerMpmdReshardToCallPass` scatters identical module-hierarchy checks and symbol-visibility boilerplate across passes.

Adding `MakeOutlinedCalleeSymbolRef`, `GetCalleeRootSymbolOp`, `GetOutlinedAtomProgramModule`, and `CloneOutlinedAtomProgramModule` in `ifrt/ir/utils` provides shared primitives for resolving and privately cloning one-level outlined atom-program modules, allowing those outlining and compilation passes to drop their local module-lookup and cloning helpers.

display_title: PR #52820: [XLA:GPU] Work around large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

head_commit.message:
PR #52820: [XLA:GPU] Work around large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52820

📝 Summary of Changes
Fixes #48979, a JAX/XLA regression.

Large POSIX-FD CUDA VMM allocations can fail with OUT_OF_MEMORY on WSL
despite sufficient free memory. Try the full allocation first, then retry
eligible WSL failures with backing allocations of at most 1 GiB mapped into
one contiguous address range.

Back contiguous device allocations with 1 GiB physical chunks on WSL
when POSIX-FD handles are enabled and fabric/multicast are unavailable.
This avoids the driver failure for large exportable allocations while
preserving sharing support.

Preserve POSIX-FD exportability for multi-GPU sharing. Other platforms keep
their existing allocation path. Locality-domain allocations, enabled FABRIC
handles, and multicast-capable devices are excluded from chunk retries.

Adds a manual 6 GiB plus padding allocator regression and a two-GPU NCCL
large-buffer registration/transfer test. Both check data around every GiB
boundary; the allocator test also checks POSIX-FD handle properties.

Disabling enable_posix_fd_handle would be a shorter workaround, but would
remove POSIX-FD export needed by cross-process GPU sharing and some NCCL
paths. Keep exportable allocations to preserve multi-GPU support under WSL2.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No perf improvements

🧪 Unit Tests:

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight allocator tests, the 6 GiB regression,
formatting, and error-injection checks pass. Three locality-domain tests
skip for version/hardware requirements. The two-GPU NCCL test compiled but
skipped on this one-GPU host. RDMA-enabled cases were not run.

🧪 Execution Tests:
None
Copybara import of the project:

--
f275b8d7a9cb1f9759df96721d88a31dced53613 by Frederic Bastien <fbastien@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Retry large exportable VMM allocations on WSL

WSL can reject large POSIX-FD VMM allocations with OUT_OF_MEMORY despite
sufficient free memory. Try the full-size allocation first, then retry
with backing chunks of at most 1 GiB on WSL with fabric handles disabled
and multicast unsupported. Exclude locality-domain allocations and map the
chunks into one contiguous virtual address range.

Keep POSIX-FD exportability to preserve multi-GPU support under WSL2.
Disabling enable_posix_fd_handle would be shorter, but removes handles
needed by cross-process GPU sharing and some NCCL paths.

Retain only the original first handle and release later creation
references after mapping. Track the mapped prefix for rollback and keep
the existing deallocation path.

Add a manual 6 GiB plus padding allocator regression and a WSL-only NCCL
regression that registers independent 6 GiB buffers, transfers the full
buffer, and checks both sides of each 1 GiB boundary. Skip the NCCL test
before GPU discovery on other operating systems and retain hardware,
memory, and chunking checks.

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight non-RDMA allocator tests, the manual
6 GiB regression, clang-format 17.0.6, and git diff --check pass. Three
upstream locality tests skip for version or hardware requirements. The
full two-GPU NCCL test skips on this single-GPU machine. Earlier local
two-process probes transferred a 6 GiB chunked source into an independent
256 MiB receiver; write and forced peer-read paths passed. The read probe
refreshed source registration per window and confirmed two-segment
imports at all five boundaries. Distinct-GPU execution remains untested.

--
086dc8783f684df908450b7e3d9e70ef491080a1 by Frederic Bastien <fbastien@nvidia.com>:

Document that a loop is only used for WSL.

--
8f33fe6191c28d8be4f5cf05a85c53a8d7fe0d4e by Frederic Bastien <fbastien@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Clarify WSL retries and generalize the NCCL regression

Make the large-buffer NCCL registration test check allocation, registration,
and full-buffer transfer across supported CUDA hosts without requiring WSL
or a particular physical mapping shape. Remove the unused detection and
mapping dependencies.

Use individual eligibility checks inside the WSL retry path, preserving
original status codes and messages while explaining why retries are not
eligible. Return non-OOM allocation failures directly and explicitly guard
the chunk-mapping loop with IsWsl().

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds, eight allocator tests, the manual 6 GiB
regression, clang-format 17.0.6, and git diff --check pass. Fault injection
confirms original non-OOM errors are returned and neither native Linux nor
failed OS detection triggers chunk retries. Three locality-domain tests skip
for version/hardware requirements. The two-GPU NCCL regression compiles but
skips on this single-GPU host; RDMA-enabled cases were not run.

Merging this change closes #52820

head_commit.message:
Hoist loop-invariant call frame fields out of `Kernel::Launch` in `xla/backends/cpu/runtime/kernel.cc`.

Synchronous `Kernel::Launch` reconstructed `XLA_CPU_NumWorkGroups`, `XLA_CPU_WorkGroupId`, and `XLA_CPU_KernelCallFrame` on every inner `(z, y, x)` iteration. Hoist `dim` and `call_frame` outside the nested loops and update only the active coordinate at each loop level (+34 bytes `.text` in `kernel.pic.o`, 0 net lines).

Problem:    Triton rejects NVFP4 (F4E2M1FN with F8E4M3FN block-16 scales)
            scaled dots on Blackwell+.
Solution:   Allow block-16 NVFP4 scaled dots in IsTritonSupportedScaledDot.

display_title: [XLA:XTile] Accumulate integer dots in output type on CPU

head_commit.message:
[XLA:XTile] Accumulate integer dots in output type on CPU

Default GEMM accumulator type selection falls back to `f32` for integer dot types such as `s32` or `u32`, which forces unnecessary float conversions and loses integer precision on CPU.

display_title: Tweak cuBLASLt fission estimation

head_commit.message:
Tweak cuBLASLt fission estimation

Etimate runtime across all supported cuBLASLt epilogues, scale the isolated Triton dot estimate by 0.80 when all matrix dimensions are at least 128, and add a 5 us offset on pre-Blackwell GPUs (0 us on Blackwell and newer).

A combination of correcting real systemic estimation errors and benchmaxxing

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Move service/gpu/model to backends/gpu/cost_model

The GPU cost models (performance models, latency estimators, interpolators,
HLO op profiles) are a GPU backend component and belong under backends/gpu
alongside codegen, transforms and autotuner, rather than in the legacy
service/gpu tree.

This is a pure move: file contents are unchanged apart from include paths,
BUILD labels and header guards.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018156196
